title: Big Axions
summary: We introduce big axions: axion models in which a Nambu-Goldstone mode emerges from the collective spontaneous breaking of a network of U(1) symmetries delocalized in theory space. Big axions naturally realize high-quality accidental global symmetries, admit both pre- and post-inflationary cosmological histories, and exhibit rich topological structures that interpolate between ordinary Peccei-Quinn axions and axions which descend from extra-dimensional gauge fields. We identify a minimal phenomenologically viable subclass, little big axions, and demonstrate that they provide a robust solution to the strong charge-parity problem in quantum chromodynamics while potentially accounting for some or all of the dark matter of the universe.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces "big axions," a new class of axion models where a Nambu-Goldstone mode arises from collective spontaneous breaking of a network of U(1) symmetries delocalized in theory space, offering high-quality accidental symmetries and rich topological structures.
AI.motivation: To generalize axion models by delocalizing U(1) symmetries across theory space, enabling high-quality accidental global symmetries and interpolating between ordinary Peccei-Quinn axions and extra-dimensional gauge field axions.
AI.method: Construction of big axion models via collective spontaneous breaking of a network of U(1) symmetries in theory space, with a minimal subclass called "little big axions" identified for phenomenological viability.
AI.result: Big axions admit both pre- and post-inflationary cosmological histories, exhibit rich topological structures, and little big axions provide a robust solution to the strong CP problem while potentially explaining some or all of dark matter.
AI.conclusion: Little big axions are a phenomenologically viable subclass that solves the strong CP problem and can account for dark matter, bridging the gap between ordinary PQ axions and extra-dimensional axions.

title: The Future of Lepton Flavor
summary: The flavor puzzle remains one of the biggest open questions in particle theory to date and upcoming results from neutrino experiments will have a large impact on its potential solution in the future. While some classes of leptonic flavor models are difficult to constrain with current data, this will change in the coming years as several yet unknown quantities, like the neutrino mass ordering and the octant of $θ_{23}$, will be determined, and the CP-violating quantity $δ$ will be measured with some precision. In addition, significant improvements in the precision of the other oscillation parameters, notably $θ_{12}$, is also expected to impact our understanding of flavor. Together with anticipated improvements on the absolute neutrino mass scale determination from the combination of cosmological data sets or beta decay endpoint spectrum measurements, upcoming experiments will lead to a refined picture of our understanding of flavor in the lepton sector. In this paper, we show exactly how flavor model predictions relate to expected measurements. Five popular classes of leptonic flavor model predictions are considered: mass sum rules, one and two texture-zeros for both Dirac and Majorana neutrinos, charged lepton corrections, modular symmetries, and constrained sequential dominance. We discuss correlations, degeneracies, and discrimination capabilities in the context of the expected measurements from upcoming experiments. We also highlight how different flavor model predictions can be differentiated and the roles each upcoming observable has on flavor model predictions. We anticipate that the precision targeted in future measurements will be sufficient to dramatically reduce the number of viable leptonic flavor models, will allow us to disentangle them, and could hopefully begin to shed light on the answer to the flavor puzzle.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes how upcoming neutrino experiments will constrain five popular classes of leptonic flavor models (mass sum rules, texture zeros, charged lepton corrections, modular symmetries, and constrained sequential dominance), showing that expected improvements in measuring neutrino mass ordering, θ₂₃ octant, CP-violating δ, θ₁₂ precision, and absolute neutrino mass scale will dramatically reduce the number of viable models and help disentangle them.
AI.motivation: The flavor puzzle remains a major open question in particle theory, and while current data struggles to constrain many leptonic flavor models, upcoming neutrino experiments will measure key unknown quantities (mass ordering, θ₂₃ octant, δ) and improve precision on other parameters, potentially discriminating between model classes.
AI.method: The authors examine five classes of leptonic flavor model predictions — mass sum rules, one/two texture-zeros (Dirac and Majorana), charged lepton corrections, modular symmetries, and constrained sequential dominance — and analyze correlations, degeneracies, and discrimination capabilities in the context of expected measurements from upcoming experiments.
AI.result: The precision targeted in future measurements will be sufficient to dramatically reduce the number of viable leptonic flavor models and allow disentangling between different model classes, with each observable playing a distinct role in constraining different model predictions.
AI.conclusion: Upcoming experimental results will significantly refine our understanding of flavor in the lepton sector and could begin to shed light on the flavor puzzle by eliminating many currently viable models.

title: Heavy-element paleodetectors for Higgsino dark matter
summary: Paleodetectors have been proposed as a new approach to direct detection of weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs), through the search for damage tracks in ancient minerals induced by WIMP-nucleon scattering. However, for inelastic dark matter such as the Higgsino, existing paleodetector targets lack sufficiently heavy nuclei to overcome the kinematic threshold for scattering. We propose heavy-element paleodetectors as a new probe of inelastic dark matter, using ancient, radiopure minerals containing heavy elements such as lead. We identify brine precipitates from deep geothermal aquifers as a possible geological source of such minerals. Additionally, paleodetectors are uniquely sensitive to the history of the dark matter high-velocity tail, including a possible fast population induced by the Large Magellanic Cloud's close approach 50 Myr ago. Such a scenario would favor younger minerals than usually assumed in the paleodetector literature. This method can probe Higgsino mass splittings up to $δ\simeq 920$ keV. Due to the large Higgsino-nucleon cross section, we find that even suboptimal mineral samples with ordinary radioactivity from depths of only 2 km can probe new parameter space, thus partially relaxing the stringent requirements on radiopurity and depth that constitute two significant challenges for the paleodetector program.

AI.tldr: Heavy-element paleodetectors using ancient lead-rich minerals from deep geothermal brines can probe inelastic dark matter (Higgsino) by overcoming kinematic thresholds, detecting high-velocity DM tails from the LMC's flyby 50 Myr ago, and relaxing radiopurity/depth requirements due to large cross sections.
AI.motivation: Standard paleodetector targets lack sufficiently heavy nuclei to overcome the kinematic threshold for inelastic dark matter (e.g., Higgsino) scattering, motivating the need for heavy-element paleodetectors.
AI.method: Proposes using ancient, radiopure minerals containing heavy elements (e.g., lead) from brine precipitates in deep geothermal aquifers. Analyzes sensitivity to DM high-velocity tail and Higgsino mass splittings.
AI.result: Can probe Higgsino mass splittings up to δ ~ 920 keV; suboptimal samples with ordinary radioactivity at 2 km depth can still probe new parameter space due to large Higgsino-nucleon cross section.
AI.conclusion: Heavy-element paleodetectors expand the reach to inelastic DM, uniquely probe the DM velocity history, and relax stringent radiopurity/depth requirements, making the program more feasible.

title: NNLO+PS Higgs-pair production in MiNNLOPS
summary: We consider Higgs-boson pair production in gluon fusion at hadron colliders and match next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections to parton showers within the MiNNLO$_{PS}$ framework. Since the full top-quark mass dependence at this order is not available, finite top-quark mass effects are incorporated through approximations based on the exact NLO QCD result, using the available two-loop amplitude in the full theory. Specifically, the Born, single-virtual, single-real and double-real contributions are included exactly, while the real--virtual and double-virtual corrections are approximated. We consider different approximations for the latter to assess the associated uncertainties. We validate our predictions against fixed-order NNLO QCD results and compare with existing NNLO calculations matched to parton shower from GENEVA, where in some cases we find noticeable differences. Finally, we present phenomenological results for different Higgs-decay channels and variations of the trilinear Higgs coupling. Our MiNNLO$_{PS}$ generator for Higgs-boson pair production is available within the POWHEG-BOX-RES framework.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the matching of NNLO QCD corrections to parton showers for Higgs-boson pair production in gluon fusion using the MiNNLO$_{PS}$ framework, incorporating finite top-quark mass effects through approximations based on exact NLO results, and provides a public generator within POWHEG-BOX-RES.
AI.motivation: To improve the theoretical precision for Higgs-boson pair production at hadron colliders by matching NNLO QCD corrections to parton showers, while accounting for finite top-quark mass effects that are crucial for accurate phenomenological predictions.
AI.method: They use the MiNNLO$_{PS}$ framework to match NNLO QCD corrections to parton showers. Since full NNLO top-mass dependence is unavailable, they approximate the real-virtual and double-virtual corrections using exact NLO QCD results and the two-loop amplitude in the full theory, while treating Born, single-virtual, single-real, and double-real contributions exactly.
AI.result: The predictions are validated against fixed-order NNLO results, and comparisons with GENEVA-based NNLO+PS calculations show noticeable differences in some cases. The generator is made publicly available in POWHEG-BOX-RES.
AI.conclusion: They provide a fully differential NNLO+PS generator for Higgs-pair production with controlled approximations for top-mass effects, enabling phenomenological studies including different Higgs decay channels and variations of the trilinear Higgs coupling.

title: Hypergroup Symmetry in Relative Quantum Field Theories and Chiral Algebras
summary:
A QFT is said to be relative if it lives at the boundary of a topological QFT in one higher dimension. We develop a general framework for working with noninvertible symmetries of relative theories in two spacetime dimensions, extending several well-known results for absolute QFTs. We emphasize various new features which arise in the relative setting, including the role of topological surfaces of the bulk, and the appearance of hypergroups and certain generalizations of tube algebras known as dome algebras. Our formalism is particularly well-suited for studying rational chiral algebras, where it predicts that finite symmetries are in explicit one-to-one correspondence with conformal embeddings of finite index.
  We describe several implications of our framework for absolute theories. First, we explain how to "glue" together symmetries of the left- and right-moving chiral algebras of a 2D CFT to produce topological line defects of the full theory. Second, we derive a precise correspondence between boundary conditions of a 2D CFT and symmetries of its chiral algebra. This correspondence has several structural corollaries: in diagonal rational CFTs, we demonstrate that the topological line defects of the theory act transitively on its boundary conditions, and further that the identity Cardy state has the smallest $g$-function amongst all boundary conditions, including those which only preserve Virasoro symmetry.
  We conclude by illustrating our results in a variety of examples. For instance, we show that, if there exists a rational chiral algebra with central charge $c=8$ whose modular tensor category is the Drinfeld center of the Haagerup fusion category, then it must arise as the fixed points of a rank-2 hypergroup acting on the $SU(3)_1\otimes (E_{6})_1$ chiral algebra.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a general framework for noninvertible symmetries in relative QFTs (theories living at the boundary of a higher-dimensional TQFT) in 2D, introducing concepts like hypergroups and dome algebras, and applies this to rational chiral algebras, boundary conditions, and topological defects in 2D CFTs.
AI.motivation: To extend the study of noninvertible symmetries from absolute QFTs to relative QFTs (those living at the boundary of a topological QFT in one higher dimension), and to provide a unified framework for understanding symmetries in 2D rational chiral algebras and CFTs.
AI.method: The paper develops a general mathematical formalism using topological surfaces of the bulk, hypergroups, and generalized tube algebras called dome algebras. It applies this to rational chiral algebras and derives correspondences between symmetries, boundary conditions, and topological line defects in 2D CFTs.
AI.result: The formalism yields: (1) a one-to-one correspondence between finite symmetries of rational chiral algebras and conformal embeddings of finite index; (2) a method to glue left/right chiral algebra symmetries into topological line defects; (3) a precise correspondence between boundary conditions and chiral algebra symmetries; (4) transitivity of topological line defects on boundary conditions in diagonal RCFTs; (5) the identity Cardy state has the smallest g-function among all boundary conditions.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides powerful tools for analyzing relative QFTs and their symmetries, with concrete predictions such as a possible rank-2 hypergroup acting on SU(3)_1 ⊗ (E6)_1 chiral algebra to produce a Haagerup-related c=8 chiral algebra.

title: Interference effects in gluon-fusion Higgs boson production
comment: 13 pages, 2 tables, 2 figures, contribution to the LHC Higgs Working Group Report 5
summary: In this contribution we summarize recent progress in higher-order computations of signal-background interference effects in Higgs boson production via gluon fusion. The focus is on the resonance region, where interference terms are most significant relative to the pure signal contribution when the Higgs boson decay is loop-induced. We present results for the well-studied $gg \to H \to γγ$ process and for the rare $gg \to H \to Zγ$ mode. In both cases, the interference is destructive, reducing the resonant Higgs boson production rate by about 1.6\% in the diphoton channel and by roughly 3\% in the $Zγ$ decay mode.

AI.tldr: This paper summarizes recent progress in higher-order computations of signal-background interference in Higgs boson production via gluon fusion, focusing on the resonance region. Results show destructive interference reduces rates by ~1.6% for $gg \to H \to \gamma\gamma$ and ~3% for $gg \to H \to Z\gamma$.
AI.motivation: To accurately predict Higgs boson production rates via gluon fusion, signal-background interference effects must be accounted for, especially in the resonance region where loop-induced decays make interference significant relative to the pure signal.
AI.method: Higher-order computations of signal-background interference effects in Higgs production via gluon fusion, focusing on the resonance region for $gg \to H \to \gamma\gamma$ and $gg \to H \to Z\gamma$ processes.
AI.result: Destructive interference reduces the resonant Higgs boson production rate by approximately 1.6% in the diphoton channel and roughly 3% in the $Z\gamma$ decay mode.
AI.conclusion: Signal-background interference effects are non-negligible in Higgs production via gluon fusion, particularly for loop-induced decays, and higher-order computations are essential for precision predictions.

title: Kaleidoscopes, Waves and the Prepotential
summary: Isomorphic flops are topology-changing transitions connecting two diffeomorphic families of Calabi-Yau threefolds. They correspond to the generators of certain Coxeter groups acting on the moduli space. As a consequence of these symmetries, the prepotential of 4D $\mathcal{N} = 2$ Type IIA compactifications on such varieties must assemble into Coxeter-invariant functions. We construct a database of all Coxeter symmetries from isomorphic flops in Kähler-favorable CICYs. The action of the Coxeter group on the Kähler moduli space leaves a symmetric bilinear form invariant, which we interpret as a metric and construct its associated Laplace-Beltrami operator. We argue that the Coxeter-invariant functions featured in the prepotential solve the Helmholtz equation with this Laplacian, and that the prepotential can then be resummed into a decomposition in terms of eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator. The convergence rate of the raw orbit sums of worldsheet instanton contributions and the resummed expressions are complementary, with the latter sharply localizing around the first few terms in the interior of the moduli space.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs a database of Coxeter symmetries from isomorphic flops in Kähler-favorable CICYs, showing that the prepotential of 4D N=2 Type IIA compactifications forms Coxeter-invariant functions. These functions solve the Helmholtz equation with a Laplace-Beltrami operator derived from a metric invariant under the Coxeter group action. The prepotential can be decomposed into eigenfunctions of this operator, with resummed expressions localizing sharply near the first few terms in the interior of moduli space, complementing the slow convergence of raw worldsheet instanton orbit sums.
AI.motivation: To understand topology-changing transitions (isomorphic flops) connecting diffeomorphic Calabi-Yau threefolds via Coxeter symmetries, and to systematically study their impact on the prepotential of Type IIA string compactifications.
AI.method: Construct a database of Coxeter symmetries from isomorphic flops in Kähler-favorable CICYs. Derive the Coxeter group action on Kähler moduli space, identify the invariant symmetric bilinear form as a metric, and construct the associated Laplace-Beltrami operator. Decompose the prepotential into eigenfunctions of this Laplacian via Helmholtz equation.
AI.result: Coxeter-invariant functions in the prepotential solve the Helmholtz equation. The resummed expression in terms of Laplace-Beltrami eigenfunctions shows sharply localized convergence around the first few terms in the interior of moduli space, complementing the slower convergence of raw worldsheet instanton orbit sums.
AI.conclusion: The Coxeter symmetry framework provides a powerful resummation technique for the prepotential, with complementary convergence properties that enhance computational efficiency in the interior of the Kähler moduli space.

title: Gravitational Wave Imprints of a High-Quality Axion and the Origin of Flavor Hierarchies
summary: Axions, arising from an anomalous global Peccei-Quinn symmetry $U(1)_{\text{PQ}}$, offer a compelling solution to the strong CP problem but are vulnerable to Planck-suppressed operators. Gauged abelian flavor symmetries $U(1)_F$, invoked to explain the flavor hierarchies via the Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism, can naturally shield the axion from such effects, yielding an accidental high-quality flavored axion with unit domain wall number. Such constructions predict two complementary signatures: (i) flavor-changing neutral currents from $K\toπa$ decays, typically associated with high flavor scales $Λ_{\text{FN}}\gtrsim f_a$, and (ii) stochastic Gravitational Waves (GWs) sourced by the evolution and decay of gauged flavonic and axionic cosmic-string networks. In addition, global axionic strings can efficiently radiate axions, potentially accounting for the observed dark matter relic abundance. We show that the resulting characteristic plateau--valley structure in the GW spectrum provides a distinctive and powerful probe of high-quality flavored axion dark matter models, complementary to low-energy flavor experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that gauged abelian flavor symmetries can protect axions from Planck-suppressed operators, leading to high-quality flavored axion dark matter models. These models predict distinct signatures: flavor-changing neutral currents (K→πa decays) and stochastic gravitational waves from cosmic-string networks, with the GW spectrum's plateau-valley structure complementing low-energy flavor experiments.
AI.motivation: Axions from the Peccei-Quinn mechanism solve the strong CP problem but are vulnerable to Planck-suppressed operators that degrade the PQ symmetry quality. The authors seek a mechanism to naturally protect the axion from such effects.
AI.method: The authors employ gauged U(1)_F flavor symmetries via the Froggatt-Nielsen mechanism to shield the axion, yielding an accidental high-quality flavored axion. They analyze the cosmological and phenomenological consequences, including cosmic-string network evolution and GW production.
AI.result: The model predicts two complementary signatures: K→πa flavor-changing neutral currents and a characteristic plateau-valley structure in the stochastic GW spectrum from flavonic and axionic cosmic-string networks. Global axionic strings can efficiently radiate axions to account for dark matter.
AI.conclusion: The plateau-valley GW spectrum provides a powerful and distinctive probe of high-quality flavored axion dark matter models, complementary to low-energy flavor experiments, offering a multi-messenger avenue for detection.

title: The Double Well Done Doubly-Well
summary: The symmetric double-well potential is one of the simplest quantum-mechanical systems in which perturbative and non-perturbative physics are deeply entangled. Its energy levels have non-analytic expansions in inverse powers of the inter-well separation, with factorially growing coefficients, while the parity splitting is exponentially small and invisible to perturbation theory. Resurgence ties the two features together, organizing the exact spectrum into a single tightly-constrained trans-series. This paper gives a self-contained account of this trans-series from two complementary approaches: exact WKB and the Euclidean path integral, developed in a common notation with explicit calculations through the four-instanton level and three-loop order. In exact WKB, Stokes phenomena encoded in the Delabaere--Dillinger--Pham relations control the analytic continuation of the wavefunction past turning points. The quantization condition expressed in terms of Voros symbols then determines the full trans-series. The DDP relations are local and do not require knowing the global topology of the energy surface, but that surface is an elliptic curve. In the path integral, elliptic curves enter differently: the classical saddle points are doubly-periodic elliptic functions of Euclidean time, and Stokes phenomena play out within the finite-dimensional manifold of quasi-zero modes rather than through analytic continuation of the wavefunction. A Lefschetz thimble decomposition determines which saddles contribute, and the resulting partition function trans-series is much simpler than the energy trans-series: at each instanton order the $T$-dependence is a polynomial fixed by the quasi-zero-mode thimble integrals. Together, the two approaches deploy a shared mathematical infrastructure in complementary ways, showing that the double well is an ideal setting to explore resurgence.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a self-contained derivation of the energy trans-series for the symmetric double-well potential using both exact WKB (with Delabaere-Dillinger-Pham relations) and Euclidean path integral (with Lefschetz thimble decomposition) approaches, showing consistent resurgence structure through four-instanton level and three-loop order, and highlighting how elliptic curves and Stokes phenomena manifest differently in the two frameworks.
AI.motivation: To give a unified, self-contained account of the resurgence structure in the double-well potential, tying together perturbative and non-perturbative sectors, using both exact WKB and path integral formalisms with explicit calculations to high order, demonstrating the double well as an ideal resurgence laboratory.
AI.method: Two complementary approaches in a common notation: (1) exact WKB with Stokes phenomena via DDP relations and Voros symbols for quantization condition; (2) Euclidean path integral with Lefschetz thimble decomposition over doubly-periodic elliptic classical saddles and quasi-zero-mode analysis.
AI.result: Trans-series for energy levels derived through four-instanton level and three-loop order; explicit demonstration that the path integral partition function trans-series has simpler polynomial T-dependence at each instanton order compared to the energy trans-series; both formalisms yield consistent resurgence structure.
AI.conclusion: The double-well potential is an ideal setting for exploring resurgence, with exact WKB and path integral deploying shared mathematical infrastructure (elliptic curves, Stokes phenomena) in complementary ways, and the two approaches together providing a complete picture of the trans-series structure.

title: Muon-induced di-tau production as a probe of new physics
summary: The muon trident process, which involves coherent scattering to produce tau pairs, is a powerful tool for constraining dark sectors. We propose to explore this channel using future high-energy muon beams with the dedicated active-target detector, High-Energy Muon Electronic Research Apparatus (HEMERA). The detector would complement muon beam-dump searches by resolving prompt signatures and could operate from preparatory facilities involving an individual muon beam to the full Muon Collider. We illustrate its capabilities for a leptophilic scalar with Yukawa-like couplings that can mediate thermal dark matter production. With $10^{18}$ incident TeV-scale muons, even a compact 10 kg silicon-based HEMERA will extend current $B$-factory and $(g-2)_μ$ bounds by over an order of magnitude in coupling strength, providing an additional compelling motivation for the development of high-energy muon beam infrastructure.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using the muon trident process (coherent scattering producing tau pairs) with a future active-target detector called HEMERA at high-energy muon beams to constrain dark sectors. With 10^18 TeV-scale muons, a compact 10 kg silicon detector could extend current bounds on leptophilic scalar mediators by over an order of magnitude in coupling strength.
AI.motivation: To explore the muon trident process as a new channel for probing dark sectors, leveraging future high-energy muon beam infrastructure (from preparatory facilities to a Muon Collider) with a dedicated detector (HEMERA) that complements existing beam-dump searches by resolving prompt signatures.
AI.method: Proposes using the High-Energy Muon Electronic Research Apparatus (HEMERA), a compact 10 kg silicon-based active-target detector, at high-energy muon beams. The detector resolves prompt signatures from muon trident production of tau pairs mediated by a leptophilic scalar, allowing sensitivity beyond traditional beam-dump experiments.
AI.result: With 10^18 incident TeV-scale muons, HEMERA can extend current B-factory and (g-2)_μ bounds on the leptophilic scalar coupling strength by over an order of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: The muon trident channel with HEMERA provides a compelling additional physics motivation for developing high-energy muon beam infrastructure, from preparatory facilities to a full Muon Collider.

title: String dualities and wedge singularities
summary: We study strings propagating in backgrounds with a wedge singularity, namely whose internal sector describes a wedge sum of closed manifolds. We focus on the wedge sum of two circles, which was recently argued to provide a quantum geometry for an M-theoretic description of type 0 strings, along with a much wider non-supersymmetric duality web stemming from quotients thereof. In the context of this proposal, we investigate whether the worldsheet features of type IIA strings, together with strong-coupling ingredients, can consistently reproduce the expectation of a weakly coupled type 0A frame. To this end, we combine worldsheet effects due to the wedge singularity with the emergence proposal applied to D0-branes probing it. We find that the resulting potential reproduces the correct tree-level mass of the tachyon in a specific scaling limit. We also discuss the possibility of kinematic obstructions to our worldsheet approach using the framework of topological modular forms, and comment on some puzzles and open questions.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates string propagation in wedge-singularity backgrounds, focusing on a wedge sum of two circles proposed as the M-theory dual of type 0 strings. By combining worldsheet effects from the wedge singularity with the emergence proposal for D0-branes, the authors reproduce the correct tree-level tachyon mass in a scaling limit, and discuss potential kinematic obstructions via topological modular forms.
AI.motivation: To test whether worldsheet features of type IIA strings, combined with strong-coupling ingredients, can consistently reproduce the expected weakly coupled type 0A frame within the wedge-singularity background proposal, thereby supporting the M-theoretic description of type 0 strings.
AI.method: The study combines worldsheet effects from the wedge singularity with the emergence proposal applied to D0-branes probing the background. It also employs topological modular forms to analyze possible kinematic obstructions.
AI.result: The potential derived from the combined worldsheet and emergence approach reproduces the correct tree-level tachyon mass in a specific scaling limit.
AI.conclusion: The worldsheet approach is consistent with the weakly coupled type 0A frame expectation in the scaling limit, though kinematic obstructions and open questions remain to be addressed.

title: BSMArt 2: simpler and faster parameter space scans
comment: 72 pages, including code listings and figures
summary: We present version 2 of BSMArt, a powerful yet lightweight scanning tool designed to simplify the exploration of parameter spaces of new physics models. Aside from architectural improvements, simpler installation and expanded documentation with examples, the new version includes additional tools and new machine learning and Monte Carlo scanning algorithms: Affine MC, Contour Finding, MLScanner, DLScanner, MLS, and CMA-ES. We showcase two variants of CMA-ES scans with physics applications relevant for soft lepton excesses at the LHC. We demonstrate that it is easily possible to find diverse and interesting parameter points for future testing.

AI.tldr: BSMArt v2 is a lightweight scanning tool for exploring new physics parameter spaces, featuring architectural improvements, expanded documentation, new ML and Monte Carlo scanning algorithms, and demonstrated application to soft lepton excesses at the LHC.
AI.motivation: To simplify and accelerate the exploration of parameter spaces in beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics models, making scanning more accessible and efficient.
AI.method: The tool adds new scanning algorithms including Affine MC, Contour Finding, MLScanner, DLScanner, MLS, and CMA-ES, alongside architectural improvements and expanded documentation.
AI.result: Demonstrates two variants of CMA-ES scans for soft lepton excesses at the LHC, showing it can efficiently find diverse and interesting parameter points.
AI.conclusion: BSMArt v2 enables easy discovery of viable parameter points for future testing in BSM physics models.

title: Unitarity, Recursion and Soft Limits in (EA)dS through Dressing
summary: Using the recently developed framework in which cosmological correlators in (E)AdS are represented as flat-space amplitudes dressed by auxiliary propagators, we show that several structural properties of the cosmological observables have a direct flat-space origin. We derive cosmological cutting rules for spinning correlators from the flat-space optical theorem, obtain the cosmological tree theorem from the Feynman tree theorem, and uplift BCFW recursion relations to (E)AdS via dressing. We also show that flat-space soft theorems reproduce the soft limits of (E)AdS correlators, and find indications of an emergent universal structure in subleading soft limits. These results provide evidence that key features of cosmological correlators can be systematically understood as dressed manifestations of flat-space physics.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that cosmological correlators in (E)AdS can be understood as dressed flat-space amplitudes, deriving cutting rules, tree theorem, BCFW recursion, and soft theorems from flat-space physics.
AI.motivation: To understand cosmological correlators' structural properties by connecting them to flat-space amplitudes through a dressing framework.
AI.method: Using the recently developed framework where cosmological correlators in (E)AdS are represented as flat-space amplitudes dressed by auxiliary propagators.
AI.result: Derived cosmological cutting rules from flat-space optical theorem, cosmological tree theorem from Feynman tree theorem, BCFW recursion relations uplifted to (E)AdS, and flat-space soft theorems reproducing soft limits of (E)AdS correlators, with evidence of emergent universal structure in subleading soft limits.
AI.conclusion: Key features of cosmological correlators can be systematically understood as dressed manifestations of flat-space physics.

title: Diffractive open charm photoproduction in ultraperipheral lead-lead and proton-lead collisions at the LHC
summary: We calculate diffractive $D^{0}$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral lead--lead (Pb--Pb) collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) within the recently developed G$γ$A--FONLL framework, where photon--lead diffraction is modeled using nuclear diffractive parton distributions obtained in the leading twist shadowing approach and the photon fluxes include corrections for independent electromagnetic dissociation accompanying the hard photoproduction process. We then use the predicted diffractive cross section to quantify the coherent diffractive contribution rejected by the $Xn0n$ neutron-tagged event selection adopted in the first measurement of $D^0$ photoproduction in Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC, which requires neutron emission from only one of the two lead nuclei. In this work, we also extend the G$γ$A--FONLL framework to proton--lead ($p$--Pb) UPCs and present predictions for inclusive and diffractive $D^{0}$ photoproduction at the LHC. In this case, the dominant configuration is photon emission from the lead ion followed by photon--proton scattering, and the diffractive contribution is evaluated using proton diffractive parton distributions constrained by HERA data.

AI.tldr: The paper calculates diffractive D⁰ photoproduction in ultraperipheral Pb-Pb and p-Pb collisions at the LHC using the GγA-FONLL framework. It quantifies the coherent diffractive contribution excluded by the Xn0n neutron-tagged selection in Pb-Pb, and extends predictions to p-Pb collisions where photon-lead interactions produce diffractive contributions via proton diffractive PDFs from HERA.
AI.motivation: To quantify the coherent diffractive contribution that is rejected by the Xn0n neutron-tagged event selection used in the first LHC measurement of D⁰ photoproduction in Pb-Pb collisions, and to extend the GγA-FONLL framework to p-Pb UPCs for inclusive and diffractive predictions.
AI.method: The GγA-FONLL framework is used: photon-lead diffraction is modeled with nuclear diffractive parton distributions from leading twist shadowing; photon fluxes include corrections for independent electromagnetic dissociation. For p-Pb, the dominant process is photon emission from lead followed by photon-proton scattering, with diffractive contributions evaluated using proton diffractive PDFs constrained by HERA data.
AI.result: Quantification of the coherent diffractive contribution removed by the Xn0n event selection in Pb-Pb, and predictions for inclusive and diffractive D⁰ photoproduction cross sections in both Pb-Pb and p-Pb UPCs at the LHC.
AI.conclusion: The GγA-FONLL framework successfully describes diffractive D⁰ photoproduction in UPCs; the Xn0n selection rejects a significant coherent diffractive component; the framework extends naturally to p-Pb collisions with HERA-constrained proton diffractive PDFs.

title: Krylov Complexity: Flat bands and Carroll breaking deformations
summary: Systems with flat band structures, when written in the language of Compact Localised States (CLS), have been shown to be explicitly invariant under supertranslation symmetries, making Carrollian symmetries inherently important for such systems. In this work, we explore the state dynamics of these systems, focusing on quenches induced by Carroll breaking perturbations, through the probe of Krylov (spread) Complexity. We specialise to Fermionic ladder Hamiltonians with all bands flat (ABF) scenario, augmented by a supertranslation preserving interaction, and discuss Krylov state complexity for quenches across critical lines. We further discuss how the growth of Krylov complexity sharply resolves the phase-dependent resilience of Carrollian sectors against delocalising perturbations. This is augmented by a complementary mechanism for Krylov growth in a continuum Carroll scalar field theory with a gradient deformation, which exhibits strong ultraviolet sensitivity (UV/IR mixing).

AI.tldr: This paper explores Krylov (spread) complexity in flat band systems with Carrollian symmetries, studying quenches induced by Carroll-breaking perturbations in Fermionic ladder Hamiltonians and a continuum Carroll scalar field theory, showing how Krylov complexity resolves phase-dependent resilience of Carrollian sectors against delocalizing perturbations.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics and resilience of Carrollian symmetries in flat band systems under symmetry-breaking perturbations, using Krylov complexity as a probe.
AI.method: Krylov (spread) complexity analysis for quenches across critical lines in Fermionic ladder Hamiltonians with all bands flat (ABF) and supertranslation-preserving interactions, complemented by continuum Carroll scalar field theory with gradient deformation.
AI.result: Krylov complexity growth sharply resolves phase-dependent resilience of Carrollian sectors against delocalizing perturbations; continuum theory exhibits strong UV/IR mixing.
AI.conclusion: Krylov complexity is an effective probe for studying Carrollian symmetry dynamics and resilience in flat band systems under symmetry-breaking perturbations.

title: Pion structure in Holographic QCD
summary: We employ a holographic model with a modified background that incorporates effective descriptions of key QCD features, including linear confinement and gluon condensation, to study the pion's internal structure, encompassing its mass spectrum as well as electromagnetic and gravitational form factors. This model is capable of simultaneously describing these diverse observables and reaches reasonable agreement with both experimental measurements and lattice QCD results. Our findings indicate that the model captures essential aspects of the pion. The description of multiple structure observables supports its potential as a useful tool for further investigations of pion properties.

AI.tldr: A holographic QCD model with modified background describing linear confinement and gluon condensation is used to study the pion's mass spectrum, electromagnetic and gravitational form factors, achieving reasonable agreement with experimental and lattice QCD results.
AI.motivation: To develop a unified holographic framework that simultaneously describes multiple aspects of pion internal structure, including mass spectrum and form factors, bridging QCD features like confinement and gluon condensation with observable pion properties.
AI.method: A holographic model employing a modified background that incorporates effective descriptions of linear confinement and gluon condensation is used to compute the pion's mass spectrum, electromagnetic form factors, and gravitational form factors.
AI.result: The model simultaneously describes pion mass spectrum, electromagnetic, and gravitational form factors, achieving reasonable agreement with experimental measurements and lattice QCD results, demonstrating its capability to capture essential aspects of the pion.
AI.conclusion: The model successfully captures essential pion properties across multiple observables, supporting its potential as a useful tool for further investigations of pion structure.

title: Mass-Flow Invariance of $Q$-Cohomology in BMN Matrix Quantum Mechanics
summary: We study the dependence of the dynamical supercharges of BMN matrix quantum mechanics on the mass parameter $μ$. Taking the $μ$-derivative at fixed canonical matrix variables, we show that the sixteen-component supercharge evolves by the adjoint action of a Hermitian quadratic bosonic operator $\mathcal{K}$, together with the spinor-space factor $iγ^{123}$. After projection to a $γ^{123}$-eigenspace, this flow integrates to a finite similarity transformation. For the nilpotent component $Q(μ)=\mathcal Q^4_-(μ)$, one obtains $Q(μ)=M(μ,μ_0)Q(μ_0)M(μ,μ_0)^{-1}$, giving an algebraic mass-flow non-renormalization statement for the $Q$-cohomology. The corresponding Hilbert-space statement has an analytic qualification, parallel to Witten's argument for supersymmetric quantum mechanics: $M$ is non-unitary and unbounded, so its action on the normalizable domain must be controlled. We formulate a small-step criterion by comparing the quadratic growth of $M$ with the Gaussian falloff of BMN oscillator wavefunctions within each component $μ>0$ or $μ<0$. As a concrete check, we evaluate this condition in the $N=2$ theory, whose two vacuum sectors are built on the trivial vacuum and the irreducible fuzzy-sphere vacuum. We also compute the induced $Q_{\rm BPS}$-action on the corresponding BPS letters: in the trivial sector it agrees with the standard BMN-sector BPS-letter differential of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, while in the irreducible sector it vanishes.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how dynamical supercharges in BMN matrix quantum mechanics depend on the mass parameter μ, showing that the flow can be integrated to a similarity transformation for the nilpotent component Q, leading to a non-renormalization statement for Q-cohomology, with a concrete check in the N=2 theory.
AI.motivation: To understand the dependence of dynamical supercharges on the mass parameter μ in BMN matrix quantum mechanics and establish a non-renormalization result for the Q-cohomology under mass flow.
AI.method: Taking μ-derivative at fixed canonical variables, showing the supercharge evolves via adjoint action of a Hermitian quadratic bosonic operator K with spinor factor iγ¹²³. Projecting to a γ¹²³-eigenspace integrates the flow to a finite similarity transformation. A small-step criterion is formulated comparing quadratic growth of M with Gaussian falloff of BMN oscillator wavefunctions.
AI.result: The nilpotent component Q(μ) satisfies Q(μ)=M(μ,μ₀)Q(μ₀)M(μ,μ₀)⁻¹, giving an algebraic mass-flow non-renormalization statement. In the N=2 theory, the induced Q_BPS-action on BPS letters agrees with the standard BMN-sector BPS-letter differential of N=4 SYM in the trivial sector, and vanishes in the irreducible fuzzy-sphere vacuum sector.
AI.conclusion: The mass-flow non-renormalization holds algebraically for Q-cohomology, with analytic qualifications needed due to the non-unitary and unbounded nature of M. The small-step criterion provides a control condition, verified in the N=2 theory.

title: QCD Sum Rule Analysis of a Compact $D^{+}D^{-}K^{+}$-Like Hidden-Charm Hexaquark with $J^{P}=0^{-}$
summary: In this work, we study a compact hexaquark configuration motivated by the same quark content as $D^{+} D^{-} K^+$ using QCD sum rules, where the $D D K$ system has been extensively studied within theoretical frameworks of few-body hadronic dynamics and coupled-channel interactions. The state is constructed from three color-octet quark--antiquark clusters coupled to an overall color singlet. We construct six independent local interpolating currents with the quantum numbers $J^{P}=0^{-}$ and analyze the corresponding two-point correlation functions. Both perturbative contributions and nonperturbative condensates up to dimension ten are included in the operator product expansion. Our analysis indicates that, within Borel windows satisfying standard sum rule criteria and with a reasonable choice of continuum threshold, the mass of the $J^{P}=0^{-}$ hidden-charm hexaquark state is estimated to be in the range $3.94$--$4.41~\mathrm{GeV}$. This prediction can provide a valuable theoretical reference for identifying such exotic hidden-charm hexaquark state in future experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper uses QCD sum rules to study a compact hexaquark state with the same quark content as $D^{+} D^{-} K^+$, predicting its mass in the range 3.94–4.41 GeV for $J^{P}=0^{-}$.
AI.motivation: To study a compact hexaquark configuration motivated by the $D D K$ system, which has been extensively studied in few-body hadronic dynamics and coupled-channel frameworks, and to provide a theoretical reference for identifying such exotic hidden-charm hexaquark states in future experiments.
AI.method: QCD sum rules analysis with six independent local interpolating currents (color-octet quark-antiquark clusters coupled to overall color singlet) for $J^{P}=0^{-}$; two-point correlation functions computed with perturbative contributions and nonperturbative condensates up to dimension ten; Borel windows with standard sum rule criteria and continuum threshold choice.

AI.conclusion: This prediction provides a valuable theoretical reference for identifying such exotic hidden-charm hexaquark states in future experiments.

title: Non-linear evolution of five-dimensional black strings in effective field theory
summary: We use numerical relativity to study the non-linear instability of five-dimensional black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Black strings evolve into a series of black holes joined by thinner string-like segments, but key features of the dynamics depend on the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. For positive coupling, favored by UV considerations, the growth of curvature invariants is limited within the validity of effective field theory (EFT), suggesting a mechanism for restoring weak cosmic censorship. For negative coupling this cap is absent and curvatures may grow until the EFT breaks down.

AI.tldr: This paper uses numerical relativity to study black string instability in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, finding that positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling caps curvature growth within effective field theory bounds, potentially preserving weak cosmic censorship, while negative coupling allows unbounded curvature growth that breaks the EFT.
AI.motivation: To investigate the non-linear instability of five-dimensional black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity and understand how the Gauss-Bonnet coupling sign affects curvature dynamics and the validity of effective field theory.
AI.method: Numerical relativity simulations of five-dimensional black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, analyzing the evolution and curvature invariants for both positive and negative Gauss-Bonnet coupling.
AI.result: Black strings evolve into black holes connected by thinner string segments. Positive coupling caps curvature growth within EFT validity, while negative coupling allows unbounded curvature growth leading to EFT breakdown.
AI.conclusion: Positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling may provide a mechanism for restoring weak cosmic censorship by limiting curvature growth within EFT bounds, whereas negative coupling leads to uncontrolled curvature divergence.

title: Probing Quantum Numbers and Decay Branching Ratios of Exotic States via Entanglement-Enabled Spin Interference
summary: Ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions (UPCs) coherently photo-produce vector mesons through two spatially separated and quantum-mechanically indistinguishable production sites, whose separation far exceeds the lifetime of the created resonance. The superposition of these amplitudes generates production-site entanglement, observed experimentally as entanglement-enabled spin-interference patterns in the angular distributions of the decay products. We show that these interference signatures provide a sensitive probe of spin-alignment transfer in hadronic decay chains, enabling intermediate-state quantum numbers and relative branching ratios to be measured from observed angular modulations. Using the decay $ρ(1450)\!\rightarrow\!π^{+}π^{-}π^{+}π^{-}$ as example, we simulate the $a_{1}(1260)π$, $h_{1}(1170)π$, $ρ(ππ)_{S}$, and $π(1300)π$ channels and demonstrate that each produces a distinct azimuthal $\cos 2φ$ modulation. The $π(1300)π$ mode shows a uniquely separated response, allowing its branching fraction to be extracted directly. These results establish production-site entanglement in UPCs as a selective tool for hadron spectroscopy, particularly for broad or overlapping resonances that are otherwise difficult to disentangle.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that quantum entanglement from two spatially separated production sites in ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions (UPCs) can be used as a tool for hadron spectroscopy. Using ρ(1450)→4π decay channels as an example, the authors demonstrate that different intermediate states produce distinct azimuthal modulations, enabling extraction of branching fractions and quantum numbers even for broad or overlapping resonances.
AI.motivation: To develop a selective spectroscopic tool for disentangling broad or overlapping hadronic resonances, which are difficult to study using conventional methods.
AI.method: The study uses production-site entanglement in UPCs, where two indistinguishable production sites separated beyond the resonance lifetime create spin-interference patterns in angular distributions of decay products. The authors simulate four decay channels of ρ(1450)→4π: a₁(1260)π, h₁(1170)π, ρ(ππ)_S, and π(1300)π, analyzing their azimuthal cos2φ modulation signatures.
AI.result: Each intermediate channel produces a distinct azimuthal cos2φ modulation pattern. The π(1300)π mode shows a uniquely separated response, allowing direct extraction of its branching fraction. The entanglement-enabled spin-interference patterns serve as sensitive probes of spin-alignment transfer in hadronic decay chains.
AI.conclusion: Production-site entanglement in UPCs provides a selective tool for hadron spectroscopy, particularly advantageous for studying broad or overlapping resonances that are otherwise challenging to disentangle. This approach enables measurement of intermediate-state quantum numbers and relative branching ratios.

title: Novel $\mathcal{N}=2$ higher-spin supercurrents
comment: 0+13 pages; In honor of the 70th anniversary of the Bogoliubov Laboratory of Theoretical Physics
summary: We study cubic interactions of $\mathcal N=2$ massless integer-spin gauge supermultiplets in harmonic superspace. We construct the complete class of abelian $(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{s_1},\mathbf{s_2})$ cubic vertices with the minimal number of space-time derivatives. Such vertices exist only for $\mathbf{s}\geq \mathbf{s_1}+\mathbf{s_2}$ and universally take the form of the gauge prepotential coupled to the conserved higher-spin supercurrent. For~$\mathbf{s_1}\neq\mathbf{s_2}$, we find the novel complex principal supercurrent, whose real and imaginary parts generate the parity-invariant and the parity-breaking interactions, respectively. The supercurrents are constructed from gauge-invariant $\mathcal N=2$ higher-spin Weyl supertensors associated with the spin-$\mathbf{s_1}$ and spin-$\mathbf{s_2}$ gauge multiplets. These supertensors are defined in terms of unconstrained higher-spin analytic prepotentials. We also derive the complete set of conserved component higher-spin currents associated with the $(s,s_1,s_2)$ vertices, including both traceless currents and currents with the non-vanishing trace.

The vertices take the form of gauge prepotential coupled to conserved higher-spin supercurrent, including a novel complex principal supercurrent for s1≠s2. The supercurrents are built from N=2 higher-spin Weyl supertensors defined via unconstrained analytic prepotentials, and the complete set of conserved component higher-spin currents is derived.
AI.motivation: To understand and classify cubic interactions of N=2 massless higher-spin gauge supermultiplets in harmonic superspace, which is essential for constructing higher-spin supergravity theories and exploring their consistency.
AI.method: Using harmonic superspace formalism, the authors construct abelian cubic vertices by coupling gauge prepotentials to conserved higher-spin supercurrents. They define N=2 higher-spin Weyl supertensors in terms of unconstrained analytic prepotentials and derive component higher-spin currents.
