A novel complex principal supercurrent is found for s1≠s2, with real and imaginary parts generating parity-invariant and parity-breaking interactions. The complete set of conserved component higher-spin currents (both traceless and with trace) is derived.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a systematic construction of cubic higher-spin interactions in N=2 superspace, establishing the structure of supercurrents and Weyl supertensors that govern such interactions, with implications for higher-spin supergravity.

title: Pion transitions in the Born-Oppenheimer Effective Field Theory: a long distance approach
summary: We address pion transitions involving heavy quarkonium and heavy exotic states in the Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory. Many of these states have a size similar or larger than the typical hadronic scale, and hence the usual QCD multipole expansion breaks down. Unknown low energy functions must be introduced, which at short distances must reproduce the known results of the multipole expansion. In order to determine the long distance behavior of these functions, we propose an interaction Lagrangian for pions and the QCD string. By matching the amplitudes obtained with this Lagrangian to the ones of the Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory in the static limit, we obtain the low energy functions in terms of three universal parameters. As a by product, we also obtain the light quark mass dependence of the string tension. Assuming that the low energy functions are long-distance dominated, we calculate several quarkonium-to-quarkonium and hybrid-to-quarkonium transitions. We estimate the universal constants and provide a phenomenological analysis of the most relevant transitions.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory approach to describe pion transitions involving heavy quarkonium and exotic states, using an interaction Lagrangian for pions and the QCD string to determine low-energy functions with three universal parameters, and provides phenomenological analysis of various transitions.
AI.motivation: Standard QCD multipole expansion fails for heavy quarkonium and exotic states with large size (comparable to or exceeding the hadronic scale), necessitating a new theoretical framework to describe pion transitions involving these states.
AI.method: The authors propose an interaction Lagrangian for pions and the QCD string within the Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory. By matching amplitudes in the static limit, they express low-energy functions in terms of three universal parameters, and also derive the light quark mass dependence of the string tension.
AI.result: The low-energy functions are expressed via three universal parameters; the light quark mass dependence of string tension is obtained; several quarkonium-to-quarkonium and hybrid-to-quarkonium transition amplitudes are calculated under the assumption that low-energy functions are long-distance dominated.
AI.conclusion: Universal constants are estimated, and phenomenological analysis of the most relevant pion transitions involving heavy quarkonium and exotic states is provided.

title: BPS Non-Renormalization in the BMN Matrix Model
summary: We show in the $(0+1)$-dimensional Berenstein-Maldacena-Nastase matrix model, dual to M-theory on a pp-wave background, that the coupling can be changed between any two finite, non-zero values using a special class of deformations, known as conjugation deformations. Importantly, we prove that they preserve normalizability of the states. This implies that BPS states in the model cannot lift as the couplings are varied, and hence their (unsigned) number cannot change, except at the free point and Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind point.

AI.tldr: In the BMN matrix model (dual to M-theory on pp-wave background), conjugation deformations allow changing the coupling between any two finite nonzero values while preserving state normalizability, proving BPS states cannot lift and their number cannot change except at free and BFSS points.
AI.motivation: To understand whether BPS states in the BMN matrix model can lift (change in energy or number) as the coupling is varied, and to establish non-renormalization properties of BPS states across the coupling landscape.
AI.method: Using a special class of deformations called conjugation deformations to vary the coupling in the (0+1)-dimensional BMN matrix model, and proving that these deformations preserve the normalizability of states, thereby protecting BPS states from lifting.
AI.result: Conjugation deformations can change the coupling between any two finite, non-zero values while preserving state normalizability. Consequently, BPS states cannot lift as couplings vary, and their unsigned number remains invariant, except at the free point (zero coupling) and the BFSS point (infinite coupling).
AI.conclusion: BPS states in the BMN matrix model are protected against lifting under continuous coupling deformation, with the only exceptions being the free and BFSS (infinite coupling) limits, establishing a non-renormalization theorem for BPS spectra in this M-theory dual.

title: Search for heavy Majorana neutrinos at muon-proton colliders via lepton-number-violating signals
summary: We propose a novel search strategy for heavy Majorana neutrinos based on the lepton-number-violating process $μ^{-}p \to jN \to j(\ell^{+}W^{-})$ at future muon-proton ($μp$) colliders equipped with 1 TeV muon beams and 7 TeV proton beams, yielding a center-of-mass energy of approximately 5.3 TeV. For heavy neutrinos with masses in the range $200~\text{GeV} \lesssim m_N \lesssim 1000~\text{GeV}$, this analysis targets the decay chain $N \to \ell^{+}W^{-} \to \ell^{+}jj$, producing a characteristic final state consisting of one charged lepton and three well-resolved jets. For TeV-scale Majorana neutrinos, the $W$ boson is highly boosted, such that its hadronic decay products coalesce into a prominent fat-jet ($J$) signature. We conduct comprehensive signal and background analyses that account for realistic detector effects to assess the search sensitivity. We derive the projected $2σ$ exclusion limits on the neutrino mixing parameter $|V_{\ell N}|^2$ based on two typical integrated luminosity scenarios of $100~\text{fb}^{-1}$ and $1~\text{ab}^{-1}$. The results demonstrate that the proposed search strategy can achieve constraints substantially superior to the existing bounds from the LHC and other high-energy colliders. This study demonstrates that future $μp$ colliders can provide competitive sensitivity for probing heavy Majorana neutrinos over the mass range $200~\text{GeV} \leq m_N \leq 3000~\text{GeV}$.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes searching for heavy Majorana neutrinos via the lepton-number-violating process μ⁻p → jN → j(ℓ⁺W⁻) at future muon-proton colliders (1 TeV μ, 7 TeV p, √s ≈ 5.3 TeV). For m_N ~ 200-1000 GeV, the decay N → ℓ⁺W⁻ → ℓ⁺jj yields one lepton + three jets; for TeV-scale neutrinos, boosted W bosons produce a fat-jet. Sensitivity analyses with detector effects derive 2σ exclusion limits on |V_ℓN|² for 100 fb⁻¹ and 1 ab⁻¹, showing constraints superior to LHC and other colliders over m_N ∈ [200, 3000] GeV.
AI.motivation: To explore heavy Majorana neutrinos via lepton-number-violating processes at future μp colliders, which may offer superior sensitivity compared to existing LHC constraints.
AI.method: Proposes searching for the process μ⁻p → jN → j(ℓ⁺W⁻) at a μp collider (1 TeV muon, 7 TeV proton beams, √s ≈ 5.3 TeV). For intermediate masses (200-1000 GeV), targets N → ℓ⁺W⁻ → ℓ⁺jj (one lepton + three resolved jets). For TeV-scale neutrinos, uses boosted W boson hadronic decays forming a single fat-jet (J). Includes realistic detector effects and background analysis.
AI.result: Derives projected 2σ exclusion limits on the mixing parameter |V_ℓN|² for integrated luminosities of 100 fb⁻¹ and 1 ab⁻¹. The proposed search yields constraints substantially better than existing bounds from LHC and other colliders for m_N between 200 GeV and 3000 GeV.
AI.conclusion: Future μp colliders can provide competitive sensitivity for probing heavy Majorana neutrinos across the mass range 200 GeV ≤ m_N ≤ 3000 GeV, significantly surpassing current experimental limits.

title: Carrollian holography with agentic AI: Real mass is imaginary
summary: We introduce LACIA, a verification-driven agentic AI workflow for theoretical physics, and apply it with independent human checks to construct Carrollian conformal bases. We develop the Poincare-Carrollian intertwiner as the central method. It reproduces the celestial and Carrollian conformal bases for massless particles and constructs the missing Carrollian bases for massive and tachyonic particles. The massive basis requires a complex momentum shift in scattering amplitudes.

AI.tldr: LACIA is a verification-driven AI workflow for theoretical physics that, using the Poincare-Carrollian intertwiner method, constructs Carrollian conformal bases for massive and tachyonic particles (requiring a complex momentum shift for the massive case) and reproduces existing bases for massless particles.
AI.motivation: To introduce a verification-driven AI workflow (LACIA) for theoretical physics and apply it to construct Carrollian conformal bases for all particle types (massless, massive, and tachyonic), filling gaps where bases were missing.
AI.method: The Poincare-Carrollian intertwiner is developed as the central method; LACIA is used with independent human checks; a complex momentum shift is introduced for the massive particle case.
AI.result: LACIA reproduces existing celestial and Carrollian conformal bases for massless particles and successfully constructs the previously missing Carrollian bases for massive and tachyonic particles.
AI.conclusion: The Poincare-Carrollian intertwiner, powered by the LACIA verification-driven AI workflow, provides a unified framework for constructing Carrollian conformal bases across all particle types.

title: Bulk viscosity of a binary mixture: the role of the intra-species interaction
summary: The bulk viscosity $ζ$ is a transport coefficient which is of central importance for various areas of modern physics. In particular, its determination for a mixture of more than one fluid is challenging, since it involves a complex interplay of multiple microscopic processes that operate on different time scales. Within the Chapman-Enskog framework, based on a series expansion of the Boltzmann distribution function, many previous works have derived the 1$^{\text{st}}$ order result for the $ζ$ of a mixture. However, such a result fails to reproduce relevant physical features of the system, especially when the masses of the two components are similar. In this work we improve the 1$^{\text{st}}$ order Chapman-Enskog result by deriving the $ζ$ at the 2$^{\text{nd}}$ order in the expansion. We show that this improved formula encodes many physical properties that the 1$^{\text{st}}$ order result misses: under specific conditions, the 2$^{\text{nd}}$ order result can be qualitatively and quantitatively very different from the 1$^{\text{st}}$ order one. Moreover, this result is compared against the $ζ$ evaluated within the Green-Kubo formalism, by means of a numerical solution of the Relativistic Boltzmann equation. The agreement with respect to this benchmark is significantly improved when moving from the 1$^{\text{st}}$ to the 2$^{\text{nd}}$ order CE result.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the bulk viscosity ζ for a fluid mixture at the 2nd order of Chapman-Enskog expansion, showing significant improvements over the 1st order result, especially when component masses are similar, and validating against Green-Kubo formalism and relativistic Boltzmann equation solutions.
AI.motivation: The bulk viscosity ζ is important in modern physics, but its determination for multi-fluid mixtures is challenging due to complex interplay of microscopic processes on different time scales. The existing 1st order Chapman-Enskog result fails to capture relevant physical features, particularly when the two components have similar masses.
AI.method: The authors derive the bulk viscosity at the 2nd order in the Chapman-Enskog expansion of the Boltzmann distribution function for a binary mixture, and compare it against numerical solutions of the Relativistic Boltzmann equation via the Green-Kubo formalism.
AI.result: The 2nd order formula encodes physical properties that the 1st order result misses; under specific conditions, the 2nd order result is qualitatively and quantitatively very different from the 1st order one. Agreement with Green-Kubo benchmarks is significantly improved when moving from 1st to 2nd order CE results.
AI.conclusion: The 2nd order Chapman-Enskog result provides a substantially more accurate description of bulk viscosity in mixtures, correcting the deficiencies of the 1st order approximation, particularly for components with similar masses.

title: Optical properties of gravitating strings
summary: We study the optical properties of gravitating Abelian-Higgs cosmic strings and compare them with those of the idealized infinitely thin string. We analyze the structure of the corresponding vortex solutions, characterizing their width, curvature profile, and approach to the ideal string limit. By investigating photon propagation in the string spacetime, we show that the finite core of the vortex gives rise to distinctive observational signatures absent in the ideal string approximation, including a characteristic triple-imaging configuration, strong demagnification of the central image, and a nontrivial Shapiro time delay between external and internal images. We determine how these effects depend on the parameters of the Abelian-Higgs model and show that the sign of the time delay is controlled by the ratio of the gauge boson mass to the Higgs boson mass, causing the string core to behave as either a temporal shortcut or a temporal barrier. Our results demonstrate that lensing effects can reveal information about the vortex formation and internal structure.

AI.tldr: The paper studies optical properties of gravitating Abelian-Higgs cosmic strings, finding that their finite core produces observational signatures distinct from infinitely thin ideal strings, including triple imaging, central image demagnification, and a sign-dependent Shapiro time delay controlled by the gauge-to-Higgs boson mass ratio.
AI.motivation: To understand how the finite core structure of realistic cosmic strings (beyond the idealized infinitely thin string approximation) affects their gravitational lensing signatures and to determine whether lensing observations can reveal information about the vortex internal structure and formation.
AI.method: The authors analyze vortex solutions of the gravitating Abelian-Higgs model, characterizing their width, curvature profile, and approach to the ideal string limit. They then study photon propagation in the string spacetime to compute lensing observables.
AI.result: Finite-core strings produce triple-imaging configurations, strong demagnification of the central image, and a nontrivial Shapiro time delay. The sign of the time delay is controlled by the ratio of gauge boson mass to Higgs boson mass, causing the string core to act as either a temporal shortcut or barrier.
AI.conclusion: Lensing effects can reveal information about vortex formation and internal structure, with the finite core giving rise to distinctive observational signatures absent in the ideal string approximation.

title: Vector charmonium(-like) states in the energy range of 4.1-4.6 GeV
summary: The spectrum of vector charmonium(-like) states in the 4.1-4.6 GeV energy region exhibits a long-standing tension. While the inclusive $R$-value indicates the presence of only vector charmonia that are usually interpreted as conventional states, exclusive $e^+e^-$ cross sections reveal additional structures whose parameters strongly depend on the observed final states when fitted with Breit-Wigner functions. This puzzling pattern suggests that coupled-channel and threshold effects play an essential role. In this work, we develop a unified coupled-channel framework relevant for the $1^{--}$ resonances in the considered energy region. The framework incorporates the $S$-wave open-charm channels $D\bar{D}_1$, $D^*\bar{D}_1$, and $D^*\bar{D}_2^*$, constrained by heavy-quark spin symmetry, optional bare poles corresponding to quark-model states which may be associated with the $ψ(4160)$ and the $ψ(4415)$, and final-state interaction in the $Z_c$ channels relevant for the three-body final states. We employ several benchmark models based on the constructed framework to perform simultaneous fits to the BESIII data for the cross sections of $e^+e^-\to J/ψπ^+π^-$, $h_cπ^+π^-$, $D\bar{D}^*π$, $D^*\bar{D}^*π$, $J/ψη$, and $χ_{c0}ω$, together with the available invariant-mass distributions that exhibit the $Z_c(3900)$ and $Z_c(4020)$ structures. The models differ in the number of bare seed states and the fitting strategy. We show that even the purely dynamical scheme captures the gross features of all the analyzed distributions. We therefore conclude that the nontrivial behavior of the measured line shapes in the studied energy range can be understood in terms of strong coupled-channel effects with dynamically generated poles. The inclusion of bare compact states leads to a quantitative improvement of the fit quality but does not alter this conclusion.

AI.tldr: A unified coupled-channel framework for vector charmonium(-like) states in the 4.1-4.6 GeV region shows that measured line shapes can be explained by strong coupled-channel effects with dynamically generated poles, without requiring conventional quark-model states. Including bare poles (ψ(4160), ψ(4415)) improves fit quality quantitatively but does not change this conclusion.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing tension between inclusive R-value measurements (suggesting conventional vector charmonia) and exclusive cross sections (revealing additional structures with final-state-dependent parameters) in the 4.1-4.6 GeV energy region.
AI.method: A unified coupled-channel framework incorporating S-wave open-charm channels (D\bar{D}_1, D^*\bar{D}_1, D^*\bar{D}_2^*) constrained by heavy-quark spin symmetry, optional bare poles for ψ(4160) and ψ(4415), and final-state interaction in Z_c channels. Simultaneous fits to BESIII data for multiple cross sections and invariant-mass distributions.
AI.result: The purely dynamical scheme captures the gross features of all analyzed distributions. Inclusion of bare compact states yields quantitative improvement but does not alter the conclusion that strong coupled-channel effects with dynamically generated poles explain the nontrivial line shapes.
AI.conclusion: The puzzling pattern of vector charmonium(-like) states in the 4.1-4.6 GeV region can be understood through strong coupled-channel effects with dynamically generated poles, rather than requiring interpretation as conventional quark-model states alone.

title: The spectrum of the bosonic ambitwistor string revisited
summary: We revisit the calculation of the spectrum of the bosonic ambitwistor string, understood as the BRST cohomology or, equivalently, as the semi-infinite cohomology of the $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ Lie algebra relative to the centre with values in a particular module. We work in momentum space, which allows us to work algebraically and interpret the BRST cohomology as inducing representations of the Poincaré group. In agreement with the existing literature, we find that all the cohomology resides in the massless sector, but a careful representation-theoretic analysis of the spectrum reveals, in addition to the usual massless sector of the closed bosonic string (dilaton, metric and Kalb--Ramond field), also a massless vector. We devote a large part of the paper to describing the cohomology at a massless momentum $p$ as a module over the stabiliser $H$ of $p$ in the Lorentz group, a task which is made difficult due to $H$ not acting reducibly when $p\neq 0$. This allows us to conclude that the spectrum is not unitary, forbidding the interpretation of the extra massless vector as a Maxwell field.

AI.tldr: This paper recalculates the spectrum of the bosonic ambitwistor string via BRST cohomology of the BMS₃ Lie algebra, finding all cohomology in the massless sector including an extra massless vector beyond the usual dilaton, metric, and Kalb-Ramond field. A representation-theoretic analysis over the Lorentz stabilizer shows the spectrum is non-unitary, ruling out interpreting the extra vector as a Maxwell field.
AI.motivation: To revisit the calculation of the bosonic ambitwistor string spectrum using BRST/semi-infinite cohomology of the BMS₃ Lie algebra, and to provide a careful representation-theoretic analysis of the cohomology as modules over the Lorentz stabilizer subgroup.
AI.method: BRST cohomology (semi-infinite cohomology of BMS₃ relative to the centre) in momentum space, working algebraically to interpret cohomology as inducing Poincaré group representations; detailed module analysis over the stabilizer H of a massless momentum p in the Lorentz group.
AI.result: All cohomology is massless; the spectrum contains the usual closed bosonic string massless sector (dilaton, metric, Kalb-Ramond) plus an extra massless vector. However, the non-reducible action of H when p≠0 shows the spectrum is non-unitary, forbidding the extra vector from being a Maxwell field.
AI.conclusion: The extra massless vector in the ambitwistor string spectrum cannot be interpreted as a Maxwell field due to the non-unitarity of the spectrum revealed by the representation-theoretic analysis over the Lorentz stabilizer.

title: Spin-orbit correlation of quarks within quarkonium
summary: The spin-orbit correlation (SOC) provides a unique probe into the internal spin structure of hadrons. Defined via the parity-odd (P-odd) energy-momentum tensor (EMT), this observable can remain non-vanishing even in systems where the total angular momentum is zero. In this study, we connect the formal field-theoretical definition of the SOC to a non-perturbative quantum many-body framework utilizing light-front dynamics. Furthermore, we show how the SOC can be extracted directly from the hadronic matrix elements of the P-odd EMT, establishing a pathway to access this observable within the partonic picture. As a practical application, we compute the transverse and longitudinal SOC distributions for charmonium and $B_c$ mesons. While our findings align with rough estimates based on the Clebsch-Gordan decomposition, we demonstrate that these observables yield rich, non-trivial information regarding partonic dynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper connects the formal field-theoretical definition of spin-orbit correlation (SOC) via the parity-odd energy-momentum tensor to a light-front quantum many-body framework, and computes transverse and longitudinal SOC distributions for charmonium and Bc mesons, revealing non-trivial partonic dynamics.
AI.motivation: SOC provides a unique probe into the internal spin structure of hadrons, and can remain non-vanishing even when total angular momentum is zero, motivating the need for a practical pathway to compute and extract this observable.
AI.method: The authors connect the field-theoretical definition of SOC (via P-odd EMT) to a non-perturbative light-front quantum many-body framework, and show how SOC can be extracted directly from hadronic matrix elements of the P-odd EMT within the partonic picture.
AI.result: The transverse and longitudinal SOC distributions for charmonium and Bc mesons are computed, yielding rich, non-trivial information about partonic dynamics, while qualitatively aligning with Clebsch-Gordan decomposition estimates.
AI.conclusion: SOC observables provide non-trivial insights into partonic dynamics beyond naive expectations, and the established framework enables practical extraction within the partonic picture for mesonic systems.

title: Dirichlet walls and the end of time
summary: We study evolution in Einstein-Hilbert gravity with Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on a finite surface. We argue that there are open sets of initial data where such evolutions terminate at finite times due to singularities that reach the boundary. In any dimension, the simplest such examples occur in cosmologies. However, in 2+1 dimensions we also show that Dirichlet walls initially outside a BTZ black hole can fall through the horizon, and that this also leads to generic singularities. A similar construction in higher dimensions leads to trapped surfaces that reach the wall, though the end result of such evolutions is more difficult to study.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gravitational evolution in Einstein-Hilbert gravity with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a finite surface, finding that open sets of initial data lead to finite-time termination due to boundary-reaching singularities, with examples in cosmologies, BTZ black holes in 2+1 dimensions, and trapped surfaces in higher dimensions.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics and potential breakdown of general relativity with Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed on a finite surface, particularly whether such evolutions can persist indefinitely or terminate in singularities.
AI.method: Analytical study of Einstein-Hilbert gravity with Dirichlet boundary conditions on a finite surface, analyzing initial value problems in cosmologies (any dimension), BTZ black hole backgrounds (2+1 dimensions), and higher-dimensional trapped surface constructions.
AI.result: Open sets of initial data lead to finite-time singularity formation that reaches the boundary; Dirichlet walls initially outside a BTZ black hole fall through the horizon, generating generic singularities; higher-dimensional constructions yield trapped surfaces reaching the wall, though endpoint analysis is more complex.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational evolutions with Dirichlet boundaries generically lead to finite-time singularities, suggesting such boundary conditions may not yield well-posed long-term dynamics in Einstein-Hilbert gravity.

title: Diffusion of multiple conserved charges from entropy production
summary: We derive dissipative relativistic hydrodynamic equations in the presence of multiple conserved charges, i.e., baryon number ($B$), electric charge ($Q$), and strangeness ($S$), using the Chapman-Enskog (CE) method within the kinetic theory approach. The relativistic Boltzmann equation is solved within the relaxation-time approximation with a momentum-independent relaxation time in the collision term. We derive both first-order (Navier-Stokes limit) and second-order dissipative hydrodynamic equations. Within the kinetic theory framework, using the Boltzmann's H-theorem, and by demanding that for a dissipative system, the entropy must be produced, we find different transport coefficients at the first-order and second-order gradient expansion of the out-of-equilibrium distribution function around the local equilibrium. Apart from the well-known transport coefficients, the shear ($η$) and the bulk ($ζ$) viscosities , we also find the diffusion matrix elements ($κ_{qq^{\prime}}$) for the conserved charges $B$, $Q$ and $S$. The diffusion matrix elements ($κ_{qq^{\prime}}$) are important to model the multi-component diffusion dynamics sourced by inhomogeneous baryon stopping in the initial state of heavy-ion collisions. We estimate the temperature ($T$) and chemical potential dependence of diagonal and off-diagonal elements of the diffusion matrix elements for the (2+1) flavor quark-gluon plasma. We further estimate the ratio $κ_{qq^{\prime}}T/η$ for a wide range of temperature and chemical potentials to show the relative importance of the diffusion matrix elements compared to other transport coefficients.

AI.tldr: This paper derives relativistic dissipative hydrodynamic equations with multiple conserved charges (B, Q, S) using the Chapman-Enskog method, obtaining first- and second-order transport coefficients including diffusion matrix elements, and estimates their temperature and chemical potential dependence for (2+1)-flavor QGP.
AI.motivation: To model multi-component diffusion dynamics in heavy-ion collisions with multiple conserved charges (baryon number, electric charge, strangeness) and understand their relative importance compared to other transport coefficients.
AI.method: Chapman-Enskog method applied to the relativistic Boltzmann equation within the relaxation-time approximation (momentum-independent relaxation time); entropy production via Boltzmann's H-theorem used to derive transport coefficients at first- and second-order gradient expansion.
AI.result: Derived shear viscosity (η), bulk viscosity (ζ), and diffusion matrix elements (κ_{qq′}) for B, Q, S; estimated temperature and chemical potential dependence of both diagonal and off-diagonal diffusion matrix elements for (2+1)-flavor QGP; computed the ratio κ_{qq′}T/η over a wide range of T and chemical potentials.
AI.conclusion: The diffusion matrix elements are important for modeling multi-component diffusion in heavy-ion collisions, and the ratio κ_{qq′}T/η quantifies their relative significance compared to other transport coefficients.

title: Hodge theory and $G_4$ fluxes in weighted projective spaces: Galois action
summary:
We extend the explicit study of $G_4$-fluxes and general Hodge cycles from the ordinary Fermat sextic fourfold to tame Fermat-type hypersurfaces in weighted projective space. The main new feature in the weighted setting is that the Galois action on the cyclotomic period data need not preserve the $(2,2)$-subspace. As a consequence, the rational reconstruction of an integral self-dual class can involve additional middle-cohomology components, increasing the norm of the corresponding flux.
  We work at maximally symmetric Fermat points, where the period matrices and symmetry-invariant Hodge loci can be computed explicitly. Using Movasati's description of periods, cyclotomic period matrices, and Hermite/Smith normal form reductions, we construct the relevant integral lattices of symmetric self-dual classes in middle cohomology. This gives a controlled test of whether symmetric general Hodge cycles can satisfy the M2-brane tadpole bound.
  Our main conclusion is empirical. In the degree 12 example in $\mathbb{P}_{1,1,1,1,4,4}$, and in the degree 8 weighted example used as a comparison, the shortest computed symmetric general Hodge cycles overshoot the tadpole bound. In the degree 36 example in $\mathbb{P}_{1,1,1,9,12,12}$, which has $h^{1,1}=11$, the most general example we have, the tadpole conjecture is indeed verified at the maximally symmetric locus, although the computations get difficult and computationally expensive.
  These computations suggest that, in weighted Fermat examples, the relevant notion of a ``symmetric flux'' must take into account not only automorphisms of the variety but also the Galois action on the period field. Non-uniform Galois orbits provide a natural arithmetic mechanism by which symmetric Hodge classes can acquire large tadpole charge.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the study of G4-fluxes and general Hodge cycles from Fermat sextic fourfolds to weighted Fermat-type hypersurfaces, finding that symmetric general Hodge cycles often exceed the M2-brane tadpole bound due to Galois action on period data, and verifying the tadpole conjecture in a degree-36 example.
AI.motivation: To test whether symmetric general Hodge cycles (relevant for G4-fluxes in F-theory) can satisfy the M2-brane tadpole bound in weighted projective hypersurfaces, where the Galois action on cyclotomic period data introduces additional complexity compared to ordinary Fermat sextic fourfolds.
AI.method: The authors work at maximally symmetric Fermat points, compute period matrices and symmetry-invariant Hodge loci explicitly using Movasati's description of periods, cyclotomic period matrices, and Hermite/Smith normal form reductions to construct integral lattices of symmetric self-dual classes in middle cohomology.
AI.result: In the degree-12 and degree-8 weighted examples, the shortest computed symmetric general Hodge cycles overshoot the tadpole bound. In the degree-36 example (with h^{1,1}=11), the tadpole conjecture is verified at the maximally symmetric locus, though computations are expensive.
AI.conclusion: In weighted Fermat examples, symmetric flux must account for both automorphisms of the variety and Galois action on the period field. Non-uniform Galois orbits provide a natural arithmetic mechanism by which symmetric Hodge classes can acquire large tadpole charge.

title: Probing SU(2) Quark Flavor Asymmetry with W Bosons at RHIC
summary: This work examines the effects of multiple parton radiation on proton-proton $W^\pm$ boson production at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC), focusing on the ratio of charged lepton pseudorapidity differential cross sections to test the SU(2) flavor symmetry violation in the proton quark sea. I show that the measured ratio is minimally affected by the fiducial constraints imposed on the QCD recoil radiation by the STAR experiment, and that the ratio is also stable with respect to transverse momentum resummation effects. Hence, the STAR data on the $W^+/W^-$ cross section ratio provides a robust discrimination of $\bar{d}(x)$ and $\bar{u}(x)$ parton distribution functions (PDFs) at momentum fractions of order 0.1, shown by comparing predictions with various PDF models and using the $L_2$ sensitivity analysis and reweighting methods.

AI.tldr: This paper studies multiple parton radiation effects on W± boson production at RHIC, showing that the measured W+/W- cross section ratio is robust against fiducial constraints and resummation effects, thus providing a reliable probe of SU(2) flavor symmetry violation in the proton quark sea via d̄(x) and ū(x) PDFs at x ~ 0.1.
AI.motivation: To test SU(2) flavor symmetry violation in the proton quark sea by examining the robustness of the W+/W- cross section ratio measured at RHIC against QCD radiation effects.
AI.method: Analysis of multiple parton radiation effects on W± production at RHIC, comparing predictions with various PDF models, using L2 sensitivity analysis and reweighting methods.
AI.result: The W+/W- ratio is minimally affected by fiducial constraints from QCD recoil radiation and stable against transverse momentum resummation effects, providing robust discrimination of d̄(x) and ū(x) PDFs at x ~ 0.1.
AI.conclusion: STAR data on the W+/W- cross section ratio offers a robust test of SU(2) flavor symmetry violation in the proton sea, confirming the reliability of the measurement as a PDF constraint.

title: Notes on (-2)-form symmetries
summary: We study $(-2)$-form symmetries of a $d$-dimensional quantum field theory, via a $(-1)$-form symmetry of its $(d+1)$-dimensional Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), realized by a non-genuine codimension-one defect in the SymTFT bulk attached to a spacetime-filling topological operator. Unlike a $(-1)$-form symmetry of a $d$-dimensional theory, which merely shifts a parameter of the absolute theory, a $(-2)$-form symmetry modifies the SymTFT action, and thereby relates theories whose ordinary global symmetries differ by anomaly data or by the associator data of a non-invertible symmetry. We illustrate the construction in two-dimensional toy models, three-dimensional ABJM-type theories, four-dimensional generalized Yang--Mills theory, and in a fusion-categorical example relating the non-invertible symmetries $\operatorname{Rep}(D_4)$ and $\operatorname{Rep}(Q_8)$. We then develop a club-sandwich realization, in which a quarter-gauging operation interfaces between IR phases of distinct RG flows of a common UV theory, and an alternative realization via nested discrete gauging. Finally, we present a holographic, top-down realization in which the type IIA Romans mass plays the role of a $(-2)$-form background for a three-dimensional Chern--Simons-matter theory, with shifts of the Romans mass realizing shifts of the boundary anomaly coefficients. We also discuss related constructions for coupled bulk--boundary systems.

AI.tldr: The paper studies $(-2)$-form symmetries of $d$-dimensional QFTs via $(-1)$-form symmetries in a $(d+1)$-dimensional SymTFT, realized by non-genuine codimension-one defects. These symmetries relate theories with differing anomaly/non-invertible symmetry data, demonstrated in various examples including toy models, ABJM, generalized Yang-Mills, Rep(D₄) vs Rep(Q₈) fusion categories, and a holographic realization with IIA Romans mass.
AI.motivation: To extend the understanding of higher-form symmetries to the $(-2)$-form case, which modifies the SymTFT action rather than merely shifting a parameter of the absolute theory, thereby relating theories with different ordinary global symmetries, anomaly data, or non-invertible symmetry associator data.
AI.method: The paper uses Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT) as the main framework, constructs non-genuine codimension-one defects in the SymTFT bulk attached to spacetime-filling topological operators, and illustrates the construction in multiple examples: 2D toy models, 3D ABJM-type theories, 4D generalized Yang-Mills, fusion-categorical examples (Rep(D₄) vs Rep(Q₈)), club-sandwich and nested discrete gauging realizations, and a holographic top-down realization with type IIA Romans mass.
AI.result: $(-2)$-form symmetries in $d$D QFT correspond to $(-1)$-form symmetries in the $(d+1)$D SymTFT. They are realized by non-genuine codimension-one defects attached to spacetime-filling operators. These symmetries shift anomaly coefficients, associator data of non-invertible symmetries, and connect theories in distinct RG flows. The IIA Romans mass provides a holographic realization as a $(-2)$-form background for 3D Chern-Simons-matter theory.
AI.conclusion: $(-2)$-form symmetries are a meaningful extension of the higher-form symmetry hierarchy, relating distinct global symmetry structures via modifications of the SymTFT action. They have concrete realizations in field theory, fusion categories, and holography.

title: Wave-Tide Locking in Thin Stellar Streams: A Phenomenological Mass Spectrometer for an Intermediate Ultralight Axion
summary:
We propose a phenomenological mass estimator for an intermediate ultralight axion dark-matter component using thin stellar streams. The central observation is an analytic relation linking three length scales in a fuzzy-dark-matter stream progenitor: the tidal radius of a bound dark core, its gravitational Bohr radius, and the axion de Broglie wavelength evaluated at the stripped-star velocity scale. If the stream width is (w=C_w r_{\rm t}), with (C_w=O(1)), then [
\frac{r_{\rm t}}{r_{\rm B}} ===========================
  \frac{4π^2}{C_w^2} \left(\frac{w}{λ_{\rm dB}}\right)^2 . ]
Thus (λ_{\rm dB}\sim w) automatically implies (r_{\rm t}/r_{\rm B}\sim25)--(40): the dark wave core survives well inside the tidal boundary while the extended stellar envelope is stripped into a thin stream. This wave--tide locking gives a no-simulation axion-mass estimator, [
m_a \simeq 2.69\times10^{-19},{\rm eV} \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{q_κ}\right) \left(\frac{R}{10,{\rm kpc}}\right) \left(\frac{38,{\rm pc}}{w}\right)^2 \left(\frac{w}{\ell_{\rm ripple}}\right) \left(\frac{220,{\rm km,s^{-1}}}{v_c}\right). ]
In the simplest locked case (\ell_{\rm ripple}\sim w), a homogeneous first-pass set of narrow stream widths points to (m_a) of a few (10^{-19},{\rm eV}) and hidden-core masses of a few (10^3)--(10^4M_\odot). This is not a detection claim; it is a falsifiable phenomenological test for an ultralight axion component that can be sharpened by homogeneous stream catalogs and Schrödinger--Poisson simulations.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a phenomenological mass estimator for ultralight axion dark matter using thin stellar streams, deriving an analytic relation linking tidal radius, Bohr radius, and de Broglie wavelength. It yields m_a ~ few × 10^{-19} eV without requiring simulations.
AI.motivation: To develop a simple, analytic method to estimate the mass of an ultralight axion dark-matter component using observable properties of thin stellar streams, avoiding expensive simulations.
AI.method: An analytic relation linking three length scales in a fuzzy-dark-matter stream progenitor: tidal radius (r_t), gravitational Bohr radius (r_B), and axion de Broglie wavelength (λ_dB) at the stripped-star velocity scale. The key relation is r_t/r_B = (4π²/C_w²) (w/λ_dB)², leading to a no-simulation mass estimator for m_a.
AI.result: For the simplest locked case (ℓ_ripple ~ w), homogeneous narrow stream widths imply m_a ~ few × 10^{-19} eV and hidden-core masses of ~10³–10⁴ M⊙.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a falsifiable phenomenological test for ultralight axion dark matter that can be improved with homogeneous stream catalogs and Schrödinger–Poisson simulations. No detection claim is made.

title: Charting the different phases of Yang-Mills-Chern-Simons-Higgs theories
summary: We explore Yang-Mills-Chern-Simons theories coupled to a Higgs-like field in the fundamental representation of $SU(2)$ quantized in linear covariant gauges in three Euclidean dimensions. We analyze the modifications in the analytic structure of the gluon propagator due to the elimination of infinitesimal Gribov copies. The interplay between the Higgs, the Chern-Simons and Gribov mass parameters is investigated. Two different phases are identified: a confining one, where all poles are complex, and a deconfined one, where would-be physical gluon excitation can appear. Unlike previous works, the Gribov parameter is consistently fixed by its gap equation as a function of the other mass parameters and the gauge coupling. This imposes a constraint in the parameter space and makes transparent how the competition of the mass parameters affects the relevance of the Gribov parameter for the characterization of the spectrum of the theory.

AI.tldr: This paper studies SU(2) Yang-Mills-Chern-Simons theories with a Higgs field in three Euclidean dimensions, analyzing how eliminating infinitesimal Gribov copies affects the gluon propagator's analytic structure. It identifies confining (complex poles) and deconfined (real gluon excitations) phases, with the Gribov parameter fixed self-consistently via its gap equation, revealing how mass parameters compete.
AI.motivation: To understand the interplay between Higgs, Chern-Simons, and Gribov mass parameters in three-dimensional gauge theories, particularly how Gribov copy elimination modifies the gluon propagator and phase structure.
AI.method: Yang-Mills-Chern-Simons theories with a fundamental Higgs field are quantized in linear covariant gauges in 3D Euclidean space. The Gribov parameter is fixed self-consistently via its gap equation as a function of other mass parameters and gauge coupling, rather than treated as a free parameter.
AI.result: Two phases identified: a confining phase with all complex poles, and a deconfined phase with possible physical gluon excitations. The Gribov parameter's relevance for the spectrum is constrained by the competition among mass parameters.
AI.conclusion: Self-consistent fixing of the Gribov parameter imposes constraints on parameter space, clarifying how mass competition determines the theory's spectrum and phase structure.

title: Machine Learning for Predicting the Proton Structure Function $F_2^P$ in QCD
summary: We present a comparative study of four supervised machine learning regression algorithms -- Support Vector Regression (SVR), Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) -- for predicting the proton structure function $F_2^p(x, Q^2)$ using high-precision BCDMS experimental data. Unlike conventional methods that solve the DGLAP evolution equations, our data-driven framework directly captures the complex nonlinear dynamics of partonic structure. To ensure statistical robustness, we employ $k$-fold cross-validation and perform thorough hyperparameter optimization. Our results show that the MLP and GPR models achieve superior predictive accuracy. In particular, MLP exhibits the highest sensitivity to nonlinear gradients, while SVR proves most stable against experimental uncertainties. The close convergence of training and validation metrics confirms that the models learn the underlying QCD physics without overfitting to statistical fluctuations. This work highlights the potential of ML-based regression as a complementary tool for structure function analysis and kinematic extrapolation in high-energy physics.

AI.tldr: This paper compares four ML regression models (SVR, GBR, GPR, MLP) for predicting the proton structure function F₂^p using BCDMS data, finding MLP and GPR achieve the best accuracy, with MLP most sensitive to nonlinear gradients and SVR most robust to uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To develop a data-driven framework for predicting the proton structure function F₂^p(x, Q²) that captures complex nonlinear dynamics of partonic structure without relying on conventional DGLAP evolution equations.
AI.method: Comparative study of four supervised ML regression algorithms (SVR, GBR, GPR, MLP) trained on high-precision BCDMS experimental data, using k-fold cross-validation and hyperparameter optimization.
AI.result: MLP and GPR achieve superior predictive accuracy; MLP shows highest sensitivity to nonlinear gradients while SVR is most stable against experimental uncertainties. Training and validation metrics converge closely, indicating no overfitting.
AI.conclusion: ML-based regression serves as a complementary tool for structure function analysis and kinematic extrapolation in high-energy physics.

title: On Quantum Aspects of 1-Form Symmetries I: BV-BRST Cohomology and Anomaly Polynomials
summary: We investigate the quantum aspects of gauging continuous 1-form global symmetries. In this paper, we study the BV-BRST quantization of a $U(1)$ 2-form gauge field, described geometrically by a $U(1)$ gerbe. Starting from the local Čech data of the gerbe, we construct the corresponding infinitesimal symmetry structure in terms of a Lie 2-algebroid, and show that, together with the associated exact Courant algebroid, it provides a natural geometric framework for the BV-BRST complex of this higher-form gauge theory. In this formulation, the field-ghost tower is encoded directly in the local gerbe data, and the higher Russian formula arises naturally from the relations among the connective structure, the curving, and the 3-form curvature. We further show that the resulting Čech-de Rham bicomplex provides a natural setting for anomaly descent for $U(1)$ 1-form symmetries, and illustrate the construction with explicit examples in Maxwell theory.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the BV-BRST quantization of a U(1) 2-form gauge field (U(1) gerbe) by constructing a Lie 2-algebroid and Courant algebroid framework from local Čech data, showing this naturally encodes the field-ghost tower, higher Russian formula, and anomaly descent for 1-form global symmetries, with examples in Maxwell theory.
AI.motivation: To understand the quantum aspects of gauging continuous 1-form global symmetries by developing a rigorous geometric framework for the BV-BRST quantization of higher-form gauge theories, specifically U(1) 2-form gauge fields described by gerbes.
AI.method: The authors start from local Čech data of a U(1) gerbe, construct the Lie 2-algebroid and associated exact Courant algebroid to frame the BV-BRST complex, and derive the field-ghost tower and higher Russian formula from the connective structure, curving, and 3-form curvature relations. The Čech-de Rham bicomplex is then used for anomaly descent.
AI.result: The paper demonstrates that the Lie 2-algebroid/Courant algebroid framework naturally encodes the BV-BRST complex for higher-form gauge theories, that the higher Russian formula emerges from gerbe geometry, and that the Čech-de Rham bicomplex provides a natural setting for anomaly descent of U(1) 1-form symmetries, illustrated with Maxwell theory examples.
AI.conclusion: The geometric framework of Lie 2-algebroids and Courant algebroids offers a natural and unified description for the BV-BRST quantization of higher-form gauge theories, connecting gerbe geometry to quantum field theory structures such as the field-ghost tower and anomaly descent.

title: Probing anomalous quartic gauge couplings in same-sign $W$ boson scattering with polarization and spin correlation
summary: The study of quartic couplings of electroweak gauge bosons not only provides a test of the Standard Model (SM) predictions, but also can look for signals of new physics beyond the SM. We present a comprehensive study of anomalous quartic gauge couplings in same-sign $W^\pm W^\pm$ production via vector boson scattering at the LHC. The analysis is carried out within the framework of the SM Effective Field Theory, exploiting polarization and spin-correlation effects encoded in angular asymmetries in addition to conventional kinematic observables. We demonstrate that spin-correlation asymmetries provide sensitivity to anomalous $WWWW$ interactions that is comparable to that obtained from the transverse mass distribution of the $WW$ system. By identifying a minimal set of the most sensitive asymmetries, we show that the dominant constraints on the Wilson coefficients can be captured with a reduced number of observables. A combined analysis of angular asymmetries and kinematic information leads to improved limits compared to either approach alone. The impact of unitarity considerations is also examined by imposing invariant-mass cut-offs on the $WW$ system, allowing us to determine unitarity-safe regions for the anomalous couplings.

AI.tldr: This paper studies anomalous quartic gauge couplings in same-sign W±W± production via vector boson scattering at the LHC using SM Effective Field Theory. The authors show that spin-correlation asymmetries provide sensitivity comparable to transverse mass distributions, and a combined analysis of angular asymmetries and kinematic observables yields improved constraints on Wilson coefficients. Unitarity-safe regions for anomalous couplings are also determined.
AI.motivation: To test Standard Model predictions and search for new physics beyond the SM by studying quartic couplings of electroweak gauge bosons, specifically anomalous quartic gauge couplings in same-sign W±W± production at the LHC.
AI.method: Analysis is performed within the SM Effective Field Theory framework, exploiting polarization and spin-correlation effects via angular asymmetries alongside conventional kinematic observables. A minimal set of sensitive asymmetries is identified, and invariant-mass cut-offs on the WW system are used to examine unitarity considerations.
AI.result: Spin-correlation asymmetries provide sensitivity to anomalous WWWW interactions comparable to that from transverse mass distributions. The dominant constraints on Wilson coefficients can be captured with a reduced number of observables. A combined analysis of angular asymmetries and kinematic information yields improved limits.
AI.conclusion: Combined angular asymmetry and kinematic analyses improve constraints on anomalous couplings. Unitarity-safe regions for anomalous couplings are determined by imposing invariant-mass cut-offs on the WW system.

title: Detecting Topological Transitions and Anisotropy through Multipartite Entanglement in Holographic Weyl Semimetals
summary: We study multipartite entanglement structures in the zero-temperature holographic Weyl semimetal, focusing on tripartite and four-partite structures. For strip regions, we compute the conditional mutual information, the entanglement wedge cross section, tripartite measures $κ$ and the Markov gap, multi-EWCS, and two multi-EWCS based four-partite signals $Δ$ and $g$. These quantities are studied as functions of the strip width $l$ and the tuning parameter across the topological transition. At large $l$, their $l$ dependence takes a power-law form governed by the IR scaling of the system. At fixed large $l$, all these entanglement quantities develop clear features near the critical point, showing that tripartite and four-partite entanglement structures can diagnose the topological quantum phase transition. We further study strips pointing in different directions to probe the anisotropy of the system. The anisotropic large l behavior distinguishes the nontrivial phase from the trivial phase. These results establish multipartite holographic entanglement as a sensitive, nonlocal probe of topological phase transitions and anisotropic IR physics.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates multipartite (tripartite and four-partite) entanglement structures in a holographic Weyl semimetal model, using various entanglement measures (conditional mutual information, entanglement wedge cross section, Markov gap, etc.) to diagnose topological quantum phase transitions and anisotropic IR physics. These quantities exhibit power-law scaling at large strip widths and develop clear features near the critical point, demonstrating that multipartite holographic entanglement serves as a sensitive nonlocal probe of topological phase transitions.
AI.motivation: To understand multipartite entanglement structures beyond bipartite entanglement in holographic Weyl semimetals, and to determine whether tripartite and four-partite entanglement measures can serve as diagnostic tools for topological quantum phase transitions.
AI.method: Computes conditional mutual information, entanglement wedge cross section, tripartite measures κ and Markov gap, multi-EWCS, and four-partite signals Δ and g for strip regions in a holographic Weyl semimetal. Studies these quantities as functions of strip width l and tuning parameter across the topological transition, including anisotropic strip orientations.
AI.result: At large l, quantities show power-law scaling governed by IR physics. At fixed large l, all entanglement quantities develop clear features near the critical point. Anisotropic large-l behavior distinguishes nontrivial phase from trivial phase.
AI.conclusion: Multipartite holographic entanglement is a sensitive, nonlocal probe of topological phase transitions and anisotropic IR physics in holographic Weyl semimetals.

title: Method to study $CP$ violation in $B_s^0\to K_S K^\pm π^\mp$ decays
summary: The $B_s^0\to K_S K^\pm π^\mp$ decays are of interest to test the Standard Model and search for new sources of $CP$ violation. A full study of these decays requires a tagged decay-time-dependent Dalitz-plot analysis performed simultaneously in the two final states. Such an analysis has never previously been performed. The method to carry out such an analysis, relating the amplitudes for decays to resonances in the two final-states to each other, is set out and its feasibility is demonstrated using pseudoexperiments. The sensitivity to the weak phase difference, $φ_s^{\rm eff}$, between $B_s^0 \to K_S K^*(892)^0$ decays with and without $B_s^0$-$\bar{B}_s^0$ mixing is studied. Good precision on $φ_s^{\rm eff}$ is found to be achievable with a dataset corresponding to LHCb Runs 1-3, with further improvement expected with datasets to be collected in future. The method is implemented in the Laura++ Dalitz-plot analysis package, and can be applied to other multibody decays with multiple final states.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new method for tagged decay-time-dependent Dalitz-plot analysis of $B_s^0\to K_S K^\pm π^\mp$ decays, applied simultaneously to both final states, and demonstrates its feasibility for measuring the weak phase $φ_s^{\rm eff}$ using pseudoexperiments, with good precision expected from LHCb Runs 1-3 data.
AI.motivation: The $B_s^0\to K_S K^\pm π^\mp$ decays are important for testing the Standard Model and searching for new sources of $CP$ violation, but a full tagged decay-time-dependent Dalitz-plot analysis performed simultaneously in the two final states had never been done before.
AI.method: The method relates the amplitudes for decays to resonances in the two final states to each other, and implements the approach in the Laura++ Dalitz-plot analysis package. Feasibility is demonstrated using pseudoexperiments.
AI.result: Good precision on the weak phase difference $φ_s^{\rm eff}$ is achievable with a dataset corresponding to LHCb Runs 1-3, with further improvement expected from future data.

title: Lecture notes: Introduction to the Off-shell Double Copy Program

summary: The present notes are based on a series of lectures prepared for an introductory eight-class course on the modern framework of the off-shell double copy. In the final part of the course, we explore modern approaches to reinterpreting the single and double copy within T-duality-invariant frameworks.

title: Fermion Families and Pontryagin Class: Topological Field Theory via Colour Symmetry Extension
summary: Family puzzle asks why the Standard Model (SM) features exactly 3 families of quarks and leptons. Motivated by topological constraints, we study 4-dimensional fermionic anomalies with discrete $Z_n$ symmetry, classified by the 5d spin bordism group. We show that only the group-cohomology subclass H$^5(Z_n,U(1))\cong Z_n$ can be canceled by an anomalous $Z_n$-symmetric 4d $Z_n$-gauge topological quantum field theory (TQFT), while beyond-group-cohomology $A_{Z_n} p_1$ involving the Pontryagin class $p_1$ cannot (except $n=2,3$). More generally, we prove that any cocycle $α_d\in$H$^d(Z_n,U(1))$ in odd spacetime dimension $d\ge3$ is trivialised by the symmetry extension $1\to Z_n\to Z_{n^2}\to Z_n\to 1,$ and we construct the corresponding symmetric anomalous boundary TQFT. For $d=5$ and $n=3$, this yields a Spin$\times Z_3$-symmetric 4d $Z_3$-gauge TQFT that cancels the mixed discrete $(\bf B+L)$-gauge-gravitational anomaly of the SM in the absence of 3 "sterile" right-handed neutrinos $ν_R$. We further analyze a generalized SM with $N_c$ colors and $N_f$ families and argue that missing $N_f$ copies of the $ν_R$ can be naturally replaced by that 4d anomalous $Spin\times_{Z_2^F} Z_{2 N_f,{{\bf B} + {\bf L}}}$ symmetric $Z_{N_c}$-gauge TQFT under the anomaly cancellation, via an appropriate $Z_{N_c}$-color symmetry extension construction $1\to Z_{N_c}\to Spin\times Z_{N_cN_f}\to Spin\times_{Z_2^F} Z_{2N_f}\to1$ of anomalous topological order. For minimal nonzero positive integers $N_c$ and $N_f$, we find the minimal color extensions: $N_c=3, N_f \ge 3$; $N_c=4, N_f \ge 2$; and $N_c=12, N_f \ge 6$. If we further require that an SM baryon is a fermion so $N_c$ is odd, then $Z_{N_c}=Z($SU$(N_c))$ color center, we prove 3 families and 3 colors, $N_c=N_f=3$, is the unique case that stands out. We also prove that $A_{Z_3}p_1= 0\mod3$ for the mod 3 cohomology class in an appropriate context.

AI.tldr: This paper explains why the Standard Model has exactly 3 families of quarks and leptons by analyzing discrete $Z_n$ anomalies, 5d spin bordism groups, and symmetry extension constructions, showing that anomaly cancellation via 4d $Z_n$-gauge TQFTs forces $N_c=N_f=3$ as the unique solution when the baryon is a fermion.
AI.motivation: To solve the "family puzzle" of why the Standard Model has exactly 3 families of quarks and leptons, using topological constraints from fermionic anomalies with discrete $Z_n$ symmetry.
AI.method: Classify 4d fermionic anomalies with discrete $Z_n$ symmetry via 5d spin bordism groups; show group-cohomology subclass $H^5(Z_n,U(1))$ can be canceled by anomalous TQFTs while beyond-group-cohomology terms cannot (except $n=2,3$); use symmetry extension $1\to Z_n\to Z_{n^2}\to Z_n\to 1$ to trivialize cocycles; analyze generalized SM with $N_c$ colors and $N_f$ families.
AI.result: For minimal nonzero positive integers, the minimal color extensions are $N_c=3, N_f\ge 3$; $N_c=4, N_f\ge 2$; $N_c=12, N_f\ge 6$. Requiring fermionic baryon ($N_c$ odd) uniquely selects $N_c=N_f=3$.
AI.conclusion: The Standard Model's 3 families and 3 colors emerge as the unique consistent solution from anomaly cancellation constraints, with the missing right-handed neutrinos replaced by an anomalous TQFT.

title: Chiral symmetry breaking in models with unconventional supersymmetry
summary: We investigate dynamical mass generation in a geometrically constructed gauge theory based on the super Lie algebra $su(2,2|3)$, in which gravity, Yang-Mills fields, and fermions are unified as components of a single gauge connection. The model contains no elementary scalar fields and no ad hoc four-fermion interactions. Instead, fermionic self-interactions arise unavoidably from the geometric structure of the theory, through nonminimal couplings and torsion associated with the unified connection. Upon reduction to an effective low-energy description, these interactions generate a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio--type potential that triggers chiral symmetry breaking and the formation of a fermion mass gap. In this framework, mass generation emerges as a direct consequence of the underlying gauge-geometric and algebraic structure, rather than as an independent dynamical assumption.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates dynamical mass generation in a gauge theory based on the super Lie algebra su(2,2|3), which unifies gravity, Yang-Mills fields, and fermions. Without elementary scalars or ad hoc four-fermion interactions, fermionic self-interactions arise from geometric structure (nonminimal couplings and torsion), generating a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio-type potential that triggers chiral symmetry breaking and fermion mass gap formation.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that mass generation can emerge naturally from the geometric and algebraic structure of a unified gauge theory based on su(2,2|3), without requiring elementary scalar fields or artificially introduced interactions.
AI.method: The theory is constructed geometrically using the super Lie algebra su(2,2|3) as a single gauge connection unifying gravity, Yang-Mills fields, and fermions. Fermionic self-interactions arise from nonminimal couplings and torsion inherent in the geometric framework. An effective low-energy reduction yields a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio-type potential.

AI.conclusion: Mass generation in this framework is not an independent dynamical assumption but a direct consequence of the underlying gauge-geometric and algebraic structure of the theory.

title: A note on the 2D NLSM free energy
summary: This note contains the perturbative computation of the 2D non-linear sigma model (NLSM) energy-density in a chemical potential $h$, at the fourth order in the coupling constant expansion. The result is in fully agreement with the $h\rightarrow \infty$ asymptotics extracted from the thermodynamical Bethe ansatz (TBA).

AI.tldr: This paper performs a fourth-order perturbative computation of the energy density of a 2D non-linear sigma model in a chemical potential, finding agreement with the large-h asymptotics from the thermodynamical Bethe ansatz.
AI.motivation: To verify the consistency of perturbative methods in the 2D NLSM at finite chemical potential by comparing with non-perturbative TBA results.
AI.method: Perturbative computation of the NLSM energy-density in a chemical potential h to fourth order in the coupling constant expansion.
AI.result: The fourth-order perturbative result matches the h → ∞ asymptotics derived from the TBA.
AI.conclusion: Perturbative calculations are consistent with non-perturbative TBA predictions in the large chemical potential regime.

title: Spinning bulk-to-boundary correlators in the massless theories with Poincaré symmetry
summary: We classify the bulk-to-boundary correlators for general integer-spin $s$ operators in a Poincaré-invariant theory by imposing suitable fall-off conditions near future/past null infinity. Any bulk-to-boundary correlator is a linear superposition of a set of basic tensor structures fixed by the little group \text{ISO}(2) of massless particles. We map the independent tensor structures to all possible non-crossing double-line diagrams. A further mapping of the double-line diagrams to circular diagrams shows that all independent tensor structures are tensor products of loop diagrams. By extrapolating the bulk-to-boundary correlators to boundary-to-boundary correlators, we find a rich structure for general spin-$s$ operators. Furthermore, we show that the extrapolated operator lies in a type Ib spin-$s$ multiplet representation of Carrollian conformal field theory (CCFT). This is a net representation that generated by the Wigner translation generators.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies bulk-to-boundary correlators for integer-spin s operators in Poincaré-invariant theories, mapping them to tensor structures, double-line diagrams, and circular diagrams. It shows the extrapolated boundary operators belong to type Ib spin-s Carrollian CFT representations generated by Wigner translation generators.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify and understand the structure of bulk-to-boundary correlators for general integer-spin massless fields, and to establish their connection to Carrollian conformal field theory representations.
AI.method: The authors impose fall-off conditions near null infinity, use little group ISO(2) symmetry to fix basic tensor structures, map structures to non-crossing double-line diagrams, further map to circular diagrams showing tensor products of loop diagrams, and extrapolate to boundary-to-boundary correlators.
AI.result: Independent tensor structures are mapped to non-crossing double-line and circular diagrams; the extrapolated boundary operator lies in a type Ib spin-s multiplet representation of CCFT, which is a net representation generated by Wigner translation generators.
AI.conclusion: Bulk-to-boundary correlators for any integer-spin operator can be systematically decomposed into basic tensor structures linked to diagrammatic representations, and these structures extend naturally to Carrollian CFT representations on the boundary.

title: Quantum Geometry from Area Fluctuations
summary: We construct a quantum-statistical analogue of Einstein's fluctuation argument for black-body radiation in the context of causal-diamond geometry. Starting from the phase space of a stretched horizon inside a Minkowski causal diamond, we quantize the Poisson algebra generated by the fields averaged over stretched-horizon time. We then compute the fluctuations of the averaged area density of the transverse two-spheres in a thermal state constructed in analogue with the black-body thermal state. In the null limit, where the stretched horizon approaches the causal-diamond boundary, this yields a thermal fluctuation formula of the boundary area operator that contains two terms, in direct analogue with the black-body radiation. The term quadratic in the expectation value is the ``classical'' contribution, while the linear term has the Verlinde--Zurek scaling characteristic of independent microscopic constituents. In direct analogue with Einstein's interpretation of black-body energy fluctuations as evidence for light quanta, we interpret the linear area-fluctuation term as a statistical signature of discrete quanta of geometry. This provides bottom-up evidence for quantum area degrees of freedom and supports the embadon picture of null quantum geometry.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs a quantum-statistical analogue of Einstein's fluctuation argument for black-body radiation within causal-diamond geometry, showing that area fluctuations of the causal-diamond boundary in a thermal state exhibit both a classical quadratic term and a quantum linear term (with Verlinde–Zurek scaling), the latter being interpreted as evidence for discrete quanta of geometry (embadons).
AI.motivation: To extend Einstein's fluctuation argument—originally used to infer the existence of light quanta from black-body energy fluctuations—to the geometry of causal diamonds, thereby seeking statistical evidence for discrete quantum degrees of freedom of spacetime itself.
AI.method: A quantum-statistical analogue of Einstein's fluctuation argument is constructed: starting from the phase space of a stretched horizon in a Minkowski causal diamond, the Poisson algebra of time-averaged fields is quantized; fluctuations of the area density of transverse two-spheres are computed in a thermal state analogous to black-body radiation; the null limit is taken where the stretched horizon approaches the causal-diamond boundary.
AI.result: In the null limit, the area fluctuation formula contains two terms: a quadratic term (classical contribution) and a linear term with Verlinde–Zurek scaling (characteristic of independent microscopic constituents), directly analogous to Einstein's black-body fluctuation formula.
AI.conclusion: The linear area-fluctuation term is interpreted as a statistical signature of discrete quanta of geometry, providing bottom-up evidence for quantum area degrees of freedom and supporting the embadon picture of null quantum geometry.

title: Smooth horizons from topology change in canonical quantum gravity
summary: We propose a resolution of the firewall paradox in JT gravity by incorporating topology change into canonical quantization under relational time evolution. The gravitational Hamiltonian acts on the black hole interior through a pair of pants interaction, mapping between a single interior sector and a connected two interior sector. To describe dynamics in the interior while keeping track of the exterior, we pass to an extended phase space description obtained by splitting the bulk Hilbert space across the event horizon. The split introduces boost edge modes at the horizon, which the Hawking modes become gravitationally dressed to. Covariance of the resulting crossed product algebra provides a precise gravitational realization of the firewall: a one sided boost of the interior edge mode relative to the exterior holding the matter fixed, or equivalently, a relative phase between the interior and exterior Hawking partners holding the edge modes fixed. Although each topology changing transition is exponentially suppressed, evolution over a Page time causes the connected two interior branch to dominate. One of these is the naive semiclassical interior, which we show carries a nontrivial one sided boost upon gluing the interior back to the exterior, and hence a firewall. The other interior is shown to be a zero mode of the one sided boost generator. Gluing the interior back to the exterior quotients by the gravitational constraints, which annihilates the firewall branch. On the surviving branch, we show the horizon vacuum measurement and the early radiation purity measurement become the same Dirac observable. Equivalently, we show that Page time dynamics induces a large diffeomorphism on the connected branch under which the operator algebra of the interior Hawking partner and that of the decoded early radiation are identified.

AI.tldr: The paper resolves the firewall paradox in JT gravity by showing that topology change during canonical quantization leads to two interior branches: one with a firewall (annihilated by constraints) and one without (surviving), where horizon vacuum and early radiation purity become the same observable after Page time.
AI.motivation: To resolve the firewall paradox—the inconsistency between smooth horizon predictions of semiclassical gravity and the requirement of unitary evaporation of black holes—by properly treating topology change and relational time evolution in JT gravity.
AI.method: The authors incorporate topology change (pair of pants interactions) into canonical quantization, split the Hilbert space across the horizon introducing boost edge modes, form a crossed product algebra, and analyze the dynamics under the gravitational Hamiltonian over Page time scales.
AI.result: Two interior branches emerge: one carries a nontrivial one-sided boost (firewall) but is annihilated by gravitational constraints when glued back; the other is a zero mode of the boost generator and survives. The Page-time dynamics identifies the horizon vacuum measurement with the early radiation purity measurement on the surviving branch.
AI.conclusion: The firewall paradox is resolved: the firewall branch is projected out by gravitational constraints, while the surviving branch gives a smooth horizon consistent with unitary evaporation, realized as a large diffeomorphism identifying interior and early radiation operator algebras.
